definition_zh: adj. 全等的（几何）；一致的，相符的
definition_en: matching exactly in shape, or in agreement
core_image: 两个三角形翻过来也严丝合缝地重合
scene: 两个三角形完全全等，叠在一起分毫不差。 The two triangles are congruent and match exactly when laid together.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：congruent 指全等的；句意是两个三角形完全重合。

derivatives.zh: 全等；一致
一致性
一致地
一致的

senses.title: Exactly the same shape
senses.definition: having the same size and shape
senses.definitionCN: 大小形状完全相同
senses.example: The two triangles are congruent.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个三角形全等。
senses.why: Latin congruere means to come together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 congruere 意为合到一处。

senses.title: In agreement
senses.definition: matching something else in meaning or fact
senses.definitionCN: 在意义或事实上与另一事物相合
senses.example: His actions are congruent with his words.
senses.exampleCN: 他的行动与言语一致。
senses.why: The geometric fit becomes a logical fit.
senses.whyCN: 几何上的吻合变成逻辑上的一致。

intro.en: Congruent comes from Latin congruere, to meet and agree.
intro.cn: congruent 源自拉丁语 congruere，意为相遇、相合。

items.en: The root means to fall or rush together.
items.cn: 该词根意为落到或涌到一处。

items.en: Congruere means to come together or agree.
items.cn: congruere 意为合到一处、一致。

items.en: The participle means agreeing.
items.cn: 该分词意为相合的。

items.en: English used congruent of fitting things.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语用它指相合之物。

items.en: Geometry fixed it as equal in shape.
items.cn: 十八世纪几何学固定其「形状相同」义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the congru stem; the near-meaning group names matching.
note.cn: 形近组共享 congru 词干；近义组列出相符。

entries.definition: The state of matching.
entries.definitionCN: 相合的状态。

entries.definition: Suitableness and agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 适宜与一致。

entries.definition: Failing to agree or fit.
entries.definitionCN: 不相合、不一致的。

entries.definition: Exactly alike in every way.
entries.definitionCN: 各方面完全相同。

entries.definition: Equal in amount or meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或意义相等。

entries.definition: Behaving in the same way over time.
entries.definitionCN: 长期保持一致。

entries.definition: Looking good or right together.
entries.definitionCN: 搭配得当的。

normalIntro.en: Congruent pieces fall into the same outline without a gap.
normalIntro.cn: congruent 的两块能不差分毫地落进同一轮廓。

normal.en: Congruere means to come together.
normal.cn: congruere 意为合到一处。

normal.en: Congruent shapes come together exactly.
normal.cn: 全等图形恰好重合。

normal.en: Congruent words come together in meaning.
normal.cn: 说辞与事实相合，也是一致。

normal.en: The noun is congruence.
normal.cn: 其名词是 congruence。

normal.en: In- makes it incongruent.
normal.cn: 加 in- 就成了「不相合」。

abstract.en: A lid that closes without a crack.
abstract.cn: 严丝合缝扣上的盖。

abstract.en: Two cut shapes matching perfectly.
abstract.cn: 两片恰好吻合的剪影。

abstract.en: Word and deed in one line.
abstract.cn: 言行落在同一条线上。

examples.en: Congruent triangles have equal sides and angles.
examples.cn: 全等三角形边角相等。

examples.en: The policy is congruent with the law.
examples.cn: 该政策与法律一致。

examples.en: Their accounts were congruent in every detail.
examples.cn: 他们的叙述在细节上完全一致。

root: 拉丁 con（共同）+ congruere（相合）→ congruens（相合的）→ 英语 congruent

sensesIntro.en: A fit so exact that the outlines coincide.
sensesIntro.cn: 契合到轮廓完全重合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two cut shapes closing into one outline
core.cn: 核心意象：两片剪形合成同一轮廓

branches.en: Two equal triangles laid together.
branches.cn: 叠在一起的两个等大三角形。

branches.en: A lid true to its box.
branches.cn: 与盒身严合的盖。

branches.en: A promise kept in action.
branches.cn: 在行动中兑现的承诺。

branches.en: Two reports telling one story.
branches.cn: 讲同一件事的两份报告。

branches.en: Exactness in shape or in sense.
branches.cn: 形状或意义上的精确相合。

intro.en: Congruent belongs to the group of words about fitting together.
intro.cn: congruent 属于表「吻合」的一组词。

latinIntro.en: Latin congruere is to meet or agree, and congruens is agreeing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 congruere 意为相遇、相合，congruens 意为相合的。

definition_zh: 大都市的；大都市区的；宗主国本土的；大主教辖区的；都市风格的；大都市居民
definition_en: relating to a metropolis or to the whole urban region around it
core_image: 一张通勤卡能坐地铁、城际铁路和跨区公交，票面印着整个都市圈的轮廓
scene: 一张通勤卡同时能坐地铁、城际铁路和跨区公交，票面印着整个都市圈的范围。 The metropolitan area extends far beyond the old city walls.
sceneCN: 这里 metropolitan 指「属于大都市区整体的」（第 2 个义项：涵盖中心城市与其通勤带的整个区域）；句意为这个大都市区远远超出旧城墙的范围。可辨识物件：通勤卡、地铁标志、城际列车、线路图。

pos.zh: 大都市的；大都市区的；宗主国本土的；大主教辖区的
大都市居民；大都市人（可数，复数 metropolitans）

derivatives.zh: 希腊 mētropolis（mētēr「母亲」+ polis「城」）→ 由「母城」偏移为「大都市」
metropolis 经法语 métropole → 偏移为「相对殖民地的宗主国本土」
metropolitan 的截短 → 偏移为「大都市的地铁系统」
metropolitan + -ism（名词后缀，表体系或心态）→ 偏移为「以大都市为中心的生活方式与心态」
metropolitan + -ize（动词后缀）→ 偏移为「使某地带上大都市的特征」
希腊 kosmos「世界」+ politēs「公民」→ 由「世界城」偏移为「具世界主义气质的」

senses.title: Of a metropolis
senses.definition: relating to a metropolis, its institutions or its characteristic life
senses.definitionCN: 与大都市、其机构或其特征性生活相关
senses.example: Metropolitan wages pull workers in from the smaller towns.
senses.exampleCN: 大都市的工资把周边小城的人吸了进来。
senses.why: the Greek noun mētropolitēs meant 'of a mother city', and the adjective still points to that leading city.
senses.whyCN: 希腊名词 mētropolitēs 意为「母城的」，这个形容词至今仍指向那座首位城市。

senses.title: Of the whole urban region
senses.titleCN: 大都市区的，涵盖通勤带的
senses.definition: covering the central city together with the suburbs and commuter belt around it
senses.definitionCN: 涵盖中心城以及其周边郊区与通勤带
senses.example: The metropolitan area extends far beyond the old city walls.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大都市区远远超出旧城墙的范围。
senses.why: once people commute across boundaries, the city that matters is the whole travel-to-work region, not the legal city.
senses.whyCN: 一旦人们跨边界通勤，真正起作用的城市是整个通勤区域，而不是法定城市。

senses.title: Of the imperial home country
senses.definition: in colonial usage, belonging to the home country that rules a dependent territory
senses.definitionCN: 在殖民用法中，属于统治附属地的本土国家
senses.example: Metropolitan troops were sent to hold the port.
senses.exampleCN: 宗主国本土的军队被派去守住那个港口。
senses.why: this sense keeps the original mother-city relation, viewed from the colony's side.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项保留了原初的母城关系，只是从殖民地一侧来看。

senses.title: Of an archbishop's see
senses.definition: relating to a metropolitan bishop and the province he oversees
senses.definitionCN: 与大主教及其所管辖的教省相关
senses.example: The metropolitan cathedral stands above the river.
senses.exampleCN: 大主教座堂立在河岸高处。
senses.why: church administration preserved the administrative sense of the mother city for centuries.
senses.whyCN: 教会行政把母城的行政义保留了许多世纪。

senses.title: City-styled
senses.titleCN: 都市风格的，有都市气派的
senses.definition: having the polish, scale or manners associated with a great city
senses.definitionCN: 具有与大城市相联的讲究、规模或举止
senses.example: The hotel markets a metropolitan style to provincial buyers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店向省内买家推销一种都市风格。
senses.why: a large city sets a standard of polish that others buy, so the adjective can describe a style rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: 大城市定下文雅的标准，别处来买，因此这个形容词可以描述风格而非地点。

senses.title: A city dweller
senses.definition: a person who lives in a metropolis, especially one identified with its habits
senses.definitionCN: 住在大都市的人，尤指带有其生活习惯的人
senses.example: The metropolitans rarely see the farms that feed them.
senses.exampleCN: 都市居民很少见到供养他们的农田。
senses.why: the adjective became a noun by leaving out the word person, a common path in English.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词省略掉「人」这个词而变成名词，这是英语常见的路径。

senses.title: Of a city transport network
senses.definition: naming rail, bus or police systems that serve a whole conurbation
senses.definitionCN: 指服务整个都市圈的铁路、公交或警务系统
senses.example: The metropolitan line was built before the suburbs filled in.
senses.exampleCN: 这条都市铁路线在郊区填满之前就建好了。
senses.why: infrastructure is organized at the scale of the whole region, so the adjective attaches to networks rather than to one city hall.
senses.whyCN: 基础设施按整个区域的尺度组织，因此这个形容词挂在网络上，而不是挂在某一个市政厅上。

senses.title: Of metropolitan government
senses.definition: relating to an authority that governs a city and its surrounding districts together
senses.definitionCN: 与把城市及其周边区县一并治理的机构相关
senses.example: Metropolitan planning overrode three local councils.
senses.exampleCN: 大都市层面的规划压过了三个地方议会。
senses.why: problems such as transport and water cross boundaries, so a single authority is created at that scale.
senses.whyCN: 交通与水这类问题跨越边界，因此要在那个尺度上设立单一机构。

intro.en: Metropolitan comes from Greek mētropolitēs 'of a mother city', through Late Latin metropolitanus and French métropolitain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: metropolitan 来自希腊 mētropolitēs「母城的」，经晚期拉丁 metropolitanus 与法语 métropolitain 进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mētropolitēs meant 'of a mother city', built on mētēr 'mother', polis 'city' and the suffix -itēs 'belonging to'.
items.cn: mētropolitēs 意为「母城的」，由 mētēr「母亲」、polis「城」与后缀 -itēs「属于」构成。

items.en: Polis meant 'city, citizen-body'; its deeper origin is uncertain and no single Indo-European source has been accepted.
items.cn: polis 意为「城邦、公民群体」；其更早来源不确定，也没有公认的单一印欧语来源。

items.en: Late Latin metropolitanus was used chiefly of bishops holding a mother see, which fixed the church sense in the West.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 metropolitanus 主要用于持有母座的主教，这一用法把教会义固定在了西方。

items.en: French métropolitain carried both the church and the city senses into modern languages.
items.cn: 法语 métropolitain 把教会义与城市义一并带入近代诸语言。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the adjective was attached to railways, police and planning that served whole conurbations.
items.cn: 在十九与二十世纪，这个形容词被挂到服务整个都市圈的铁路、警务与规划上。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of polis before Greek is unsettled, and the exact date of the first English use is unrecorded, so any earlier form proposed is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 来源不确定：polis 在希腊语之前的来源无定论，英语首见的确切年代也没有记录，因此凡提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the polis family and the words it is swapped with; group two holds adjectives for government and for non-metropolitan places.
note.cn: 第一组是 polis 词族及常被互换的词；第二组是表治理以及表非都市地区的形容词。

entries.definition: The city as an entity; metropolitan is the adjective for it and for its surrounding region.
entries.definitionCN: 作为实体的城市；metropolitan 是它及其周边区域的形容词。

entries.definition: The colonial power's home territory; metropolitan in its colonial sense describes what belongs to that home.
entries.definitionCN: 殖民国家的本土；metropolitan 的殖民义即描述属于那个本土的东西。

entries.definition: Of a town as a legal corporation; metropolitan covers a far larger area than any single municipality.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为法人的城镇；metropolitan 覆盖的范围远大于任何单个市镇。

entries.definition: Of a city in general; metropolitan adds the idea of the leading city and its whole commuter region.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指城市的；metropolitan 额外带上首位城市及其整个通勤区域的意思。

entries.definition: The shortened form, now mostly naming an underground railway system rather than the region.
entries.definitionCN: 截短形式，如今多指地下铁路系统，而非整个区域。

entries.definition: Relating to citizens or city government; it concerns administration, where metropolitan concerns scale and region.
entries.definitionCN: 与公民或市政府相关；它关乎行政，而 metropolitan 关乎规模与区域。

entries.definition: Made up of many peoples and outlooks; it describes mixture, not size or administration.
entries.definitionCN: 由许多民族与观念混合而成；它描述混合，而非规模或行政。

entries.definition: Of the provinces, often with a tone of narrowness; it is the standard contrast to metropolitan.
entries.definitionCN: 外省的，常带狭窄之气；它是 metropolitan 的标准对照词。

entries.definition: The city where government sits; metropolitan describes a region, which may contain the capital or not.
entries.definitionCN: 政府所在之城；metropolitan 描述的是一个区域，其中可能有也可能没有首都。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek compound, the real region phrases and the real family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊复合词、真实的区域说法与真实词族。

normal.en: mētēr 'mother' + polis 'city' + -itēs 'belonging to': belonging to the mother city.
normal.cn: mētēr「母亲」+ polis「城」+ -itēs「属于」：属于母城的。

normal.en: The family runs metropolis, metropolitan, metropole, metro, metropolitanism, cosmopolitan.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 metropolis、metropolitan、metropole、metro、metropolitanism、cosmopolitan。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: metropolitan area, metropolitan government, metropolitan railway.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：大都市区、大都市政府、都市铁路。

normal.en: Three scales: urban for the city, metropolitan for the region, provincial for everything outside.
normal.cn: 三个尺度：urban 指城市，metropolitan 指整个区域，provincial 指外面的一切。

normal.en: The church sense survives in titles such as metropolitan bishop, a bishop of a mother see.
normal.cn: 教会义仍活在 metropolitan bishop 这类称谓里，指母座主教。

abstract.en: Picture a ticket that works on every kind of transport inside one drawn ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一张票，在一个画出的圈内所有交通工具上都能用。

abstract.en: Picture a boundary drawn around commuters rather than around walls.
abstract.cn: 想象一条边界围着通勤者画，而不是围着城墙画。

abstract.en: Picture a single office that must answer for three town halls at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个办公室要同时为三个市政厅负责。

examples.en: Metropolitan growth has outpaced the water authority's planning.
examples.cn: 大都市的增长已经超过了水务部门的规划。

examples.en: The metropolitan elite rarely sends its children to local schools.
examples.cn: 都市精英很少把孩子送进本地学校。

examples.en: In colonial records, metropolitan goods were taxed less than local ones.
examples.cn: 在殖民档案里，宗主国本土货物的税比本地货物低。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「metro（母亲、大城）+ politan（属于……的）」——属于那座母城及其整个周边的 → 大都市的

root: 希腊 mētropolitēs「母城的」（mētēr「母亲」+ polis「城」+ -itēs「属于」），经晚期拉丁 metropolitanus 与法语 métropolitain；polis 更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one scale: the leading city, then the whole commuter region, then the imperial home, the church province, a city style, its residents, its networks and finally its government.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个尺度展开：先是首位城市，再是整个通勤区域，随后是宗主国本土、教省、都市风格、都市居民、都市网络，最后是都市治理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring drawn around a city wide enough to contain everyone who comes into it to work.
core.cn: 核心意象：围着城市画的一个圈，宽到足以容纳所有进来工作的人。

branches.en: CITY AND REGION: the leading city first, then the whole travel-to-work area that depends on it.
branches.cn: 城市与区域：先是首位城市，再是依赖它的整个通勤区域。

branches.en: TWO ADMINISTRATIVE HOMES: the colonial mother country and the archbishop's province both rule from a centre.
branches.cn: 两个行政母体：殖民地母国与大主教教省都从一个中心施行管辖。

branches.en: STYLE BORROWED FROM THE CENTRE: manners and scale marketed as belonging to the great city.
branches.cn: 从中心借来的风格：被当作属于大城市的举止与气派在市场上流通。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: those who live at that scale, and are identified with its habits.
branches.cn: 人：在那个尺度上生活、并被认作带有其习惯的人。

branches.en: NETWORKS AND GOVERNMENT: transport and policing are organized region-wide, and so is the authority above the councils.
branches.cn: 网络与治理：交通与警务按整个区域组织，压在议会之上的机构也是如此。

intro.en: The adjective is a Greek compound plus a Latin adjective ending, and each element still builds words in English.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是一个希腊复合词加一个拉丁形容词词尾，每个成分在英语中仍在构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin took mētropolitēs as metropolitanus, a church adjective; there is no inherited Latin root family here, only a Greek compound dressed in a Latin ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把 mētropolitēs 吸收为教会形容词 metropolitanus；这里没有拉丁固有词根词族，只有一个穿上拉丁词尾的希腊复合词。

items.example: The first element marks the parent city.
The second element names the city.
The suffix makes an adjective of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表归属的形容词。

items.example: The ending carried the word into Latin.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把这个词带进了拉丁语。

items.example: The region looks to its metropolis.
items.exampleCN: 这个区域仰赖它的大都市。
宗主国本土定下了关税。

items.example: The corridor is now a megalopolis.
items.exampleCN: 这条走廊如今已是巨型城市带。

items.example: The port has a cosmopolitan population.
items.exampleCN: 这座港口的人口来自世界各地。

items.example: Metropolitanism can blind planners to the provinces.
items.exampleCN: 都市心态会让规划者看不见外省。

definition_zh: 学会会员；院士；学者
definition_en: a member of an academy, especially one that promotes art or science
core_image: 院士证：被正式选入最高学术殿堂的人
scene: 典礼上，白发老人从院长手中接过证书，正式成为科学院的一员。 The new academician thanked the academy in his speech.
sceneCN: 这里 academician 是「院士、学会会员」（第 1 个义项：被选入学会的正式成员）；句意为新院士在致辞中感谢科学院。

collocations.phrase: an academician of the academy of sciences

derivatives.zh: 本词的基础名词，义为「学会；学院；研究院」
由 academy 派生的形容词，义为「学术的；学院的」
由 academic 加副词后缀构成，义为「在学术上」

senses.title: A member of an academy
senses.definition: a person formally elected to membership in an academy of arts or sciences
senses.definitionCN: 被正式选入艺术或科学学会的成员
senses.example: She was elected an academician at forty-five.
senses.exampleCN: 她四十五岁时当选为院士。
senses.why: The suffix -ian marks a person attached to something, so the word names one who belongs to the academy.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ian 标记「隶属于某机构的人」，所以这个词指属于学会的人。

senses.title: A scholar or teacher
senses.definition: a scholar, professor, or person connected with formal learning, sometimes with a formal or old-fashioned flavour
senses.definitionCN: 学者、教授或与正规学问相关的人，有时带书卷气
senses.example: The old academician preferred footnotes to headlines.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老学者喜欢脚注胜过头条新闻。
senses.why: Because academy came to mean formal schooling, its person-word extended to anyone living in that world of books.
senses.whyCN: 因为 academy 后来指正规学校，其「人」的称谓便扩展到任何生活在书本世界的人。

intro.en: Academician joins academy with the person suffix -ian, ultimately recalling Plato's grove of Academus.
intro.cn: academician 由 academy 加表示人的后缀 -ian 构成，最终可追溯到柏拉图讲学的阿卡德摩斯园林。

items.en: The grove where Plato taught gave Greek akademia its name.
items.cn: 柏拉图讲学的园林赋予希腊语 akademia 名称。

items.en: Latin adopted the name for the philosophical school.
items.cn: 拉丁语用该名称指这所哲学学校。

items.en: French académie named learned societies from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 académie 自十六世纪起指学术团体。

items.en: Italian formed accademico for a member of such a society.
items.cn: 意大利语造 accademico 指此类团体的成员。

items.en: English borrowed the member-word as academician.
items.cn: 英语借入该「成员」称谓为 academician。

note.en: The first group gathers the academy word family; the second gathers words for learned people.
note.cn: 第一组收 academy 词族；第二组收指学者的词。

entries.definition: Adjective for things related to schools and study.
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词，指与学校、学习相关的。

entries.definition: The society or school itself.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指学会或学院本身。

entries.definition: Adverb meaning in terms of study results.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，指在学业成绩方面。

entries.definition: A learned person, often a researcher.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学者」，常指研究者。

entries.definition: A person of deep learning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「博学之士」，书面语。

entries.definition: A senior university teacher.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大学教授」。

entries.definition: A member of a college or learned society.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「（学院或学会的）会员」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the academy root and the -ian suffix; the abstract hooks picture the election ceremony.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 academy 词根与 -ian 后缀；抽象记忆点想象当选仪式。

normal.en: Academy + -ian: the suffix marks a person.
normal.cn: academy 加 -ian：后缀标记人。

normal.en: Compare musician: a person of music, academician: a person of the academy.
normal.cn: 类比 musician（音乐之人），academician 即学会之人。

normal.en: Academies of science elect academicians formally.
normal.cn: 科学院正式选举院士。

normal.en: The stress falls on -mi-: a-ca-de-MI-cian.
normal.cn: 重音落在 -mi- 上。

normal.en: In some countries academician is an honorific title.
normal.cn: 在某些国家，院士是一种荣誉称号。

abstract.en: Picture a certificate with a gold seal naming a new member.
abstract.cn: 想象一张盖着金印的证书，写下新成员之名。

abstract.en: Picture Plato under his trees, surrounded by chosen students.
abstract.cn: 想象柏拉图在园林中，被选中的学生环绕。

abstract.en: Picture an old scholar reading until the lamp burns low.
abstract.cn: 想象老学者读书至灯油耗尽。

examples.en: The academician presented her findings at the annual meeting.
examples.cn: 这位院士在年会上展示了她的研究成果。

examples.en: Only forty academicians sit in that historic society.
examples.cn: 那个历史悠久的学会仅有四十名院士。

examples.en: As a young academician, he wrote with refreshing directness.
examples.cn: 作为年轻学者，他写作直截了当，令人耳目一新。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿卡德米先」——进了学会（academy）就是先一步的学者。

root: 希腊语 akademia（柏拉图学园，源自园林名）→ 法语 académie + 意大利语成员后缀 → 英语 academician（学会成员）

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from formal membership in an academy to any scholar living the academic life.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从学会的正式成员，扩展到任何过学术生活的学者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person holding the academy's membership seal
core.cn: 核心意象：手握学会印记的人

branches.en: One formally elected into a learned society.
branches.cn: 被正式选入学术团体的人。

branches.en: One whose daily world is books and research.
branches.cn: 日常世界是书本与研究的人。

branches.en: Both senses sit inside the academy's world of learning.
branches.cn: 两个义项都处于学园的学问世界之内。

branches.en: Membership implies election by one's peers.
branches.cn: 成员身份意味着同行的选举认可。

branches.en: The informal sense sometimes hints at bookish stiffness.
branches.cn: 宽泛义有时暗示书生气。

intro.en: The word adds the person suffix -ian to academy; the family also yields the adjective academic.
intro.cn: 这个词给 academy 加上「人」后缀 -ian；词族还派生形容词 academic。

latinIntro.en: Latin academia preserves the Greek place name, so the Latin entry records the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 academia 保留了希腊地名，拉丁条目记录该名词。

definition_zh: 辐射；散发（热、光）；流露；呈放射状散开
definition_en: to send out heat, light or feeling from a centre, or to spread outward
core_image: 一块烧红的铁把热一圈圈推向四周，越远越淡
scene: 炉子烧起来以后，热从铁皮中心一圈圈散到房间各处。 Once the stove was lit, heat began to radiate from its centre across the room.
sceneCN: 这里 radiate 指散发热量（第 1 个义项：向外辐射）；句意为炉子烧起来以后，热从铁皮中心一圈圈散到房间各处。

pos.zh: 辐射；散发；流露；呈放射状散开

derivatives.zh: 辐射；放射
散热器；暖气片
发光的；容光焕发的

senses.title: To radiate heat
senses.definition: to give off heat in all directions from a source
senses.definitionCN: 从热源向各个方向放出热量
senses.example: Once the stove was lit, heat began to radiate from its centre across the room.
senses.exampleCN: 炉子烧起来以后，热从铁皮中心一圈圈散到房间各处。
senses.why: The first sense is physical and directional.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项是物理的、有方向的。

senses.title: To radiate light
senses.definition: to send out light that spreads from a point
senses.definitionCN: 从一点向四周放出的光
senses.example: The lamp radiated a soft yellow light over the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 台灯在书桌上散出柔和的黄光。
senses.why: Light and heat share the same outward motion.
senses.whyCN: 光与热共享同一种向外的运动。

senses.title: To radiate joy
senses.definition: to show a feeling so strongly that others feel it coming from you
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地表现一种情感，别人感到它从你身上发出
senses.example: She radiated joy from the moment she entered the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她一走进房间，就流露出喜悦。
senses.why: The metaphor makes a person into a source.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把一个人变成一个光源。

senses.title: To radiate confidence
senses.definition: to give others a strong impression of assurance
senses.definitionCN: 给别人强烈的可靠感
senses.example: The young speaker radiated confidence without raising his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻演讲者没有提高音量，却流露出自信。
senses.why: The sense is social: a quality is transmitted outward.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是社会的：一种品质被向外传送。

senses.title: Radiating lines
senses.definition: lines that spread from a common point like spokes
senses.definitionCN: 像辐条一样从同一点散开的线
senses.example: The map showed roads radiating from the old market square.
senses.exampleCN: 地图上，道路从老市场广场呈放射状散开。
senses.why: Geometry keeps the shape and drops the energy.
senses.whyCN: 几何学保留形状，丢掉能量。

senses.title: Radiate from a centre
senses.definition: to spread outward in every direction from a single origin
senses.definitionCN: 从单一原点向各方向扩散
senses.example: Every rumour seemed to radiate from one small office.
senses.exampleCN: 所有传闻似乎都从那间小办公室散开。
senses.why: The sense can describe information as easily as warmth.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项描述信息，和描述温度一样容易。

senses.title: A radiating pattern
senses.definition: a design of lines or rays that run outward from a middle
senses.definitionCN: 由中心向外延伸的线或射线构成的图案
senses.example: The ceiling carried a radiating pattern of thin wooden strips.
senses.exampleCN: 天花板上有一种细木条构成的放射状图案。
senses.why: Design borrows the geometry of light.
senses.whyCN: 设计借用了光的几何。

senses.title: Versus emit
senses.definition: to spread in all directions, as opposed to sending out in one
senses.definitionCN: 向各方向散开，与朝一个方向发出相对
senses.example: A lamp emits light; a fire radiates warmth.
senses.exampleCN: 灯发出光，火散发热。
senses.why: The pair separates a beam from a glow.
senses.whyCN: 这一对词把光束与光晕分开。

intro.en: Radiate comes from Latin radiare, 'to emit rays', from radius, a spoke or ray.
intro.cn: radiate 来自拉丁语 radiare（放出射线），词根是 radius（辐条、光线）。

items.en: Radius named a spoke of a wheel and a ray of light.
items.cn: radius 指车轮的辐条，也指光线。

items.en: Radiare meant to send out rays.
items.cn: radiare 意为放出射线。

items.en: English used radiate for light and heat first.
items.cn: 英语最初用 radiate 指光与热。

items.en: Radiation became a technical term for transmitted energy.
items.cn: radiation 成为传递能量的技术术语。

items.en: The word now also describes a person who seems to glow.
items.cn: 今天这个词也描述一个仿佛在发光的人。

note.en: The look-alike group is the radi- family; the near-meaning group separates emit, diffuse, emanate and spread.
note.cn: 形近组是 radi 词族；近义组把「发出」「扩散」「散发」「传播」分开。

entries.definition: sending out light or joy.
entries.definitionCN: 发出光或喜悦的。

entries.definition: energy sent out as rays.
entries.definitionCN: 以射线形式发出的能量。

entries.definition: a device that gives off heat.
entries.definitionCN: 散发热量的装置。

entries.definition: a line from the centre to the edge.
entries.definitionCN: 从中心到边缘的线。

entries.definition: to send out light, sound or gas.
entries.definitionCN: 发出光、声或气体。

entries.definition: to spread widely through a space.
entries.definitionCN: 在空间中广泛扩散。

entries.definition: to come out from a source.
entries.definitionCN: 从某个源头流出。

entries.definition: to extend over a wider area.
entries.definitionCN: 扩展到更大范围。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a hot iron sending warmth outward in rings.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一块烧红的铁一圈圈向外送热」的画面。

normal.en: Radiate shares its root with radius and ray: everything leaves a centre.
normal.cn: radiate 与 radius、ray 同根：一切都从中心离开。

normal.en: Picture spokes on a wheel and heat travelling along each one.
normal.cn: 想象车轮上的辐条，热沿着每一根往外走。

normal.en: Say RAY-dee-ate; the first syllable sounds like ray.
normal.cn: 读 RAY-dee-ate，第一音节听起来就是 ray。

normal.en: The word moves easily from stoves to smiles.
normal.cn: 这个词从炉子移到微笑，毫不费力。

normal.en: Ask which direction: outward from a point, or straight along a beam?
normal.cn: 问方向：是从一点向外，还是沿一条光束直走？

abstract.en: To radiate is to make your centre visible.
abstract.cn: 辐射，就是让你的中心变得可见。

abstract.en: Heat, light and feeling obey one grammar: a source, a direction, a distance.
abstract.cn: 热、光与情感遵守同一套语法：一个源、一个方向、一段距离。

abstract.en: The word flatters people: it turns a mood into a form of energy.
abstract.cn: 这个词抬举人：它把一种心境变成一种能量。

sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一种运动向外送：热、光、喜悦、自信、线条、传闻、装饰，以及与直射光束的对照。
