definition_zh: 有明确目的的；有意为之的；坚定的；有意义的；专为某用途设计的
definition_en: having a clear aim, and acting or being made in a way that serves it
core_image: 一个人把散在桌上的工具一件件收进对应的格子里，动作不快，但没有一次多余
scene: 她把工具箱的每一格都按用途排好，别人取什么都能立刻找到。 A purposeful arrangement of the tools saved the crew an hour each morning.
sceneCN: 这里 purposeful 指「有明确目的、且服务于该目的」（第 1 个义项：目的明确）；句意为把工具按用途排好，每天早上为工班省下一小时。图中可辨识物件：分格的工具箱、按用途归位的扳手、没有多余动作的手、被标出的常用格。

pos.zh: 有目的的；有意为之的；坚定的；有意义的

derivatives.zh: 在形容词后加副词后缀构成，语义由「有目的的」转为「有目的地」
在形容词后加名词后缀构成，语义由「有目的的」转为「有目的性这一特质」
把表示「充满」的后缀换成表示「缺少」的后缀，语义由「有目的」转为「无目的」
基础名词，语义为「目的」，是本形容词的构词起点

senses.title: Having a clear aim
senses.definition: acting or existing with a definite aim that guides every step
senses.definitionCN: 带着一个明确目标去行动或存在，每一步都受它引导
senses.example: A purposeful arrangement of the tools saved the crew an hour each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 把工具按用途排好，每天早上为工班省下一小时。
senses.why: the suffix means full of, so a purposeful act is full of an aim rather than merely busy.
senses.whyCN: 后缀意为「充满」，因此一个有目的的行为是被目标填满的，而不是仅仅忙碌。

senses.title: Done on purpose
senses.definition: deliberately done, so that the result was intended rather than accidental
senses.definitionCN: 有意做出，因此结果是想要的，而不是碰巧的
senses.example: The gap in the wall was purposeful: it lets the cat through.
senses.exampleCN: 墙上那道缝是有意留的，好让猫通过。
senses.why: an aim that is fully present in the act makes the act deliberate, and the word marks that intent.
senses.whyCN: 目标完整地存在于行为中，这个行为就是有意的，这个词正是标出这份意图。

senses.title: Firm in carrying out
senses.definition: showing steady resolution in the way an action is carried through
senses.definitionCN: 在完成行动的方式上显出稳定的决心
senses.example: Her purposeful stride told the others the decision was final.
senses.exampleCN: 她那坚定的步伐让众人知道决定已不可更改。
senses.why: an aim held without wavering shows in the body before it shows in argument.
senses.whyCN: 一个不摇动的目标，会先显现在身体上，而不是先显现在论证里。

senses.title: Having genuine meaning
senses.definition: filled with a point that makes the effort worth making, said of work or a life
senses.definitionCN: 被一个使付出值得的意义所填满，用于工作或人生
senses.example: The years in the clinic were the most purposeful of his life.
senses.exampleCN: 在诊所的那些年是他一生中最有意义的时光。
senses.why: when the aim is large, the word stops describing acts and starts describing a whole stretch of life.
senses.whyCN: 当目标足够大，这个词就不再描述行为，而开始描述一整段人生。

senses.title: Made for one use
senses.definition: designed with a specific job in view, so that nothing is ornamental
senses.definitionCN: 带着一项具体功能来设计，因此没有多余的装饰
senses.example: The bench was purposeful: low, wide and easy to clean.
senses.exampleCN: 这条长凳是为用途而造的：低、宽、好清理。
senses.why: an aim can be built into an object, where it appears as the absence of decoration.
senses.whyCN: 目标可以被造进一件物品里，在那里它显现为「没有装饰」。

senses.title: Focused rather than scattered
senses.definition: concentrated on the aim at hand instead of drifting among tasks
senses.definitionCN: 集中在眼前的目标上，而不是在任务之间漂移
senses.example: A purposeful half hour beat a distracted afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 有目的的半小时胜过一个心不在焉的下午。
senses.why: the same filled aim shows as economy of motion, which is why the word often modifies time and work.
senses.whyCN: 同一份被填满的目标会显现为动作的节省，因此这个词常修饰时间与工作。

senses.title: Read as having a hidden intent
senses.definition: appearing to carry an intention beyond what is said, as of a glance or a pause
senses.definitionCN: 看起来带着话语之外的另一层意图，用于眼神或停顿
senses.example: There was a purposeful pause before she answered.
senses.exampleCN: 她回答之前有一个像是别有用意的停顿。
senses.why: observers read intent into small signs, and the word then describes what others infer rather than what was meant.
senses.whyCN: 观察者会从小动作里读出意图，此时这个词描述的是别人推断出的东西，而不是本人所想的。

senses.title: Serving the aim without waste
senses.definition: using only what the aim requires, with no surplus effort or material
senses.definitionCN: 只用达成目的所必需的部分，不多费一点力气或材料
senses.example: The pruning was purposeful, and the tree carried more fruit the next year.
senses.exampleCN: 那次修剪是有目的的，第二年树上的果子更多了。
senses.why: a fully present aim trims away whatever does not serve it, which is the practical face of the word.
senses.whyCN: 一个完整在场的目标会把不服务于它的部分剪掉，这是这个词在实践上的面孔。

intro.en: Purposeful is purpose plus the Old English suffix -ful 'full of'. Purpose itself comes through Old French porpos from Latin proponere 'to put forward'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: purposeful 是名词 purpose 加上古英语后缀 -ful「充满」。purpose 本身经古法语 porpos 来自拉丁 proponere「放到前面」。年代均为约数。

items.en: The suffix -ful meant 'full of, having the quality of', and it turned nouns into adjectives such as careful and useful.
items.cn: 后缀 -ful 意为「充满、具有……性质」，它把名词变成形容词，如 careful 与 useful。

items.en: The noun entered English meaning an aim or intention put before the mind, from the verb for putting something forward.
items.cn: 这个名词进入英语时指摆在心头的目标或意图，其动词意为「把某物摆到前面」。

items.en: The adjective purposeful appears in the nineteenth century, when purposeful activity became a favourite phrase of educators and reformers.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十九世纪出现，当时「有目的的活动」成了教育者与改革者爱用的说法。

items.en: Twentieth-century writing applied it to buildings and objects, where an aim shows as the absence of anything ornamental.
items.cn: 二十世纪的写作把它用于建筑与器物，那里目标显现为「没有多余装饰」。

items.en: The phrase a purposeful life treats an aim large enough to organize a lifetime as a virtue in itself.
items.cn: 「有意义的人生」这一说法，把一个大到能组织一生的目标本身当作一种德性。

items.en: Source uncertain (exact first date of the adjective): no citation fixes its first use for designed objects, and the dating of its moral use rests on printed sources only.
items.cn: 来源不确定（形容词确切的最早年代）：它首次用于器物设计没有确切书证；道德用法的年代只能依据留存印刷材料推断。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes from the same purpose family; group two separates adjectives that praise directed activity.
note.cn: 第一组区分同属 purpose 词族的形近词；第二组按赞美「有方向的活动」的方式区分形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning deliberately; it modifies the act rather than describing the actor.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「故意地」的副词；修饰行为，而不是描述行为者。

entries.definition: Without any aim, drifting; it is the direct opposite and carries a mild reproach.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无目标、漂着；是直接的反面，带轻微责备。

entries.definition: Built specifically for one use; it narrows the design sense to construction.
entries.definitionCN: 专为某一用途建造的；把设计义收窄到建筑。

entries.definition: From a verb meaning to carry: to claim or seem to mean, which is a matter of appearance rather than aim.
entries.definitionCN: 出自一个意为「搬运」的动词：声称或看似意指，说的是表象而非目标。

entries.definition: To put a plan forward; same Latin verb as purpose but no suffix of fullness.
entries.definitionCN: 把计划摆出来；与 purpose 同出那个拉丁动词，但不带「充满」的后缀。

entries.definition: Done consciously and after weighing; it stresses the choice, while purposeful stresses the aim.
entries.definitionCN: 有意识、经过权衡后做出的；强调选择，而 purposeful 强调目标。

entries.definition: Firm and not wavering in purpose; it describes the will rather than the aim's clarity.
entries.definitionCN: 目标坚定、毫不动摇；描述意志，而不是目标的清晰。

entries.definition: Having significance or value; it is the inner, felt side of what purposeful describes outwardly.
entries.definitionCN: 具有意义或价值；是 purposeful 在外在描述之下的内在感受面。

entries.definition: With attention concentrated on one thing; it describes attention, not the aim that directs it.
entries.definitionCN: 注意力集中在一处；描述注意力，而不是引导它的目标。

entries.definition: Done according to a method or system; it can be systematic without any clear purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 按方法或体系来做；可以很有体系却毫无明确目的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The suffix means full of, so a purposeful act is full of its aim rather than full of motion.
normal.cn: 后缀意为「充满」，因此有目的的行为是被目标填满，而不是被动作填满。

normal.en: The family runs purpose, purposeful, purposefully, purposefulness, purposeless.
normal.cn: 同族词覆盖名词、形容词、副词、抽象名词与否定式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: a purposeful walk, purposeful design, purposeful use of time.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：有目的的行走、有明确用途的设计、有目的地利用时间。

normal.en: The design sense shows as what is missing: a purposeful bench has no ornament at all.
normal.cn: 设计义显现为「缺了什么」：一条为用途而造的凳子，一点装饰也没有。

normal.en: The moral sense appears in a purposeful life, where the aim is large enough to organize years.
normal.cn: 道德义出现在「有意义的人生」里，那里目标大到足以组织许多年。

abstract.en: Picture a chisel laid down the moment the joint is finished.
abstract.cn: 想象接缝一做完，凿子立刻被放下。

abstract.en: Picture a route on a map with no loop and no detour.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上一条没有回环、没有绕行的路线。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp aimed at one desk while the rest of the room stays dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯只照一张桌子，其余房间仍是暗的。

examples.en: The workshop ran on purposeful practice, not on repetition for its own sake.
examples.cn: 这间工坊靠的是有目的的练习，而不是为重复而重复。

examples.en: Her purposeful editing cut the report by half.
examples.cn: 她那番有目的的编辑把报告删掉了一半。

examples.en: A purposeful silence followed the question, and then he answered.
examples.cn: 问题之后是一段别有用意的沉默，然后他才回答。

dict_mnemonic.text: purpose（目的）+ full（满）——被目的装满的 → 有目的的

root: purpose（古法语 porpos「目标」← 拉丁 proponere「放到前面」= pro- + ponere）+ 古英语后缀 -ful「充满」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one measure: an aim fills an act, a thing, a stretch of life or a silence, and the adjective reports how completely that aim is present.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一把尺展开：一个目标填满一个行为、一件物、一段人生或一段沉默，这个形容词报告那个目标在场得有多完整。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tools sorted into labelled compartments with no wasted motion.
core.cn: 核心意象：工具被分进标好用途的格子，没有一个多余动作。

branches.en: THE AIM PRESENT: what is done with an aim is also what is done deliberately.
branches.cn: 在场的目标：带着目标做的，也就是有意做的。

branches.en: THE AIM FELT AS WILL: steadiness of stride before any argument.
branches.cn: 目标在意志上被感到：在论证之前，先是步伐的稳定。

branches.en: THE AIM BUILT IN: a bench with no ornament and a pruning with no waste.
branches.cn: 被造进去的目标：一条无装饰的长凳，一次不浪费的修剪。

branches.en: THE AIM ORGANIZING TIME: half an hour aimed beats an afternoon adrift.
branches.cn: 组织时间的目标：有方向的半小时胜过漂着的下午。

branches.en: THE AIM READ TWICE: by the person as meaning, by others as a hidden intent.
branches.cn: 被读两次的目标：本人读作意义，旁人读作别有用意。

intro.en: The word is a borrowed noun plus a native suffix, so one half is Latin in origin and the other is English.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个借入的名词加一个本族后缀，一半源自拉丁，一半是英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere 'to place' gives propose, compose and position; the native suffix -ful also builds useful, careful and hopeful.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ponere「放置」衍生出 propose、compose 与 position；本族后缀 -ful 还构成 useful、careful 与 hopeful。

items.meaning: full of; having the quality of
items.example: A useful map folds into a pocket.
items.exampleCN: 一张实用的地图能折进口袋。

items.structure: Old French porpos, from Latin proponere
items.example: The purpose was stated in one line.
The walk was purposeful and short.
items.exampleCN: 那次行走有明确目的，而且很短。

items.example: She purposefully chose the longer route.
items.exampleCN: 她有意选了更长的那条路。

items.meaning: the quality of having an aim
items.example: The plan's purposefulness impressed the board.
items.exampleCN: 这份计划的目的性打动了董事会。
无目的的跑动让孩子累了。

items.example: A purpose-built shed held the grain.
A multipurpose room serves as both hall and clinic.
items.exampleCN: 一间多用途房既是会场也是诊所。
他们提出了一个更简的设计。

items.example: The position was marked with a stake.

definition_zh: 财政政策（政府以税收与公共支出调节经济的措施）
definition_en: the government's use of taxation and public spending to influence the economy
core_image: 两只手在同一本账簿上动作，一只手加税，一只手拨款修路
scene: 经济连续两个季度收缩，财政部提出减税并加快修路，以财政政策托住需求。 With output falling for two quarters, the treasury proposed tax cuts and faster road works as fiscal policy to support demand.
sceneCN: 这里指「政府用税收与支出来影响经济的措施」（第 1 个义项：以预算手段调节总需求）；句意为经济连续两个季度收缩，财政部提出减税并加快修路，以财政政策托住需求。可辨识物件：账簿、税单、修路图纸、公文包。

pos.zh: 作定语：财政政策的（如财政政策空间）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指各国各自的政策）

derivatives.zh: 短语的基础形容词，出自拉丁「国库的」→ 财政的
基础形容词加副词后缀 → 在财政上
短语的基础名词，经拉丁上溯希腊「城邦治理」→ 政策
基础名词加表示制定者的复合成分 → 决策者
前缀义为「收拢」加钱箱词根，再加动词后缀 → 没收

senses.title: The government's budget stance overall
senses.definition: the general direction set by a government through its taxing and spending decisions
senses.definitionCN: 政府通过征税与支出决定所定的总方向
senses.example: Fiscal policy was neutral for most of the decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这十年里的大部分时间，财政政策是中性的。
senses.why: fiscal points at the public purse and policy at a chosen course, so the phrase is the course a government chooses for its budget.
senses.whyCN: 「财政的」指向公家钱袋，「政策」指向选定的路线，合起来就是政府为预算选定的路线。

senses.title: Expansionary policy through spending or tax cuts
senses.titleCN: 以增支或减税实现的扩张性政策
senses.definition: a deliberate widening of the deficit to raise demand and employment
senses.definitionCN: 有意扩大赤字以提高需求与就业
senses.example: Expansionary fiscal policy shortened the downturn but left a larger debt.
senses.exampleCN: 扩张性财政政策缩短了低迷期，却留下更大的债务。
senses.why: if the private sector stops spending, the government can spend in its place, which is why the deficit is widened on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 如果私人部门停止支出，政府可以替它支出，因此赤字被有意扩大。

senses.title: Contractionary policy or austerity
senses.titleCN: 紧缩性政策或财政紧缩
senses.definition: a deliberate narrowing of the deficit through higher taxes or lower spending
senses.definitionCN: 通过加税或减支有意缩小赤字
senses.example: Contractionary fiscal policy was imposed as a condition of the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 紧缩性财政政策作为贷款条件被强制实施。
senses.why: the mirror image of expansion: when debt is judged too high, the chest is closed rather than opened.
senses.whyCN: 这是扩张的镜像：当债务被认为过高时，钱箱被关上而不是打开。

senses.title: Automatic stabilizers built into the budget
senses.titleCN: 预算中自带的自动稳定器
senses.definition: features such as unemployment benefits that expand or shrink without a new law
senses.definitionCN: 失业救济之类无需新立法即自动扩张或收缩的安排
senses.example: Automatic stabilizers did much of the work before any fiscal policy was voted on.
senses.exampleCN: 在任何财政政策付诸表决之前，自动稳定器已经起了大部分作用。
senses.why: some spending follows the cycle by design, so the budget stabilizes demand even when no one acts, and this is counted as part of the policy.
senses.whyCN: 有些支出按设计随周期起落，即使无人行动预算也在稳定需求，这部分也算作政策。

senses.title: Discretionary measures voted in a downturn
senses.titleCN: 衰退中经表决的相机抉择措施
senses.definition: one-off decisions such as a stimulus package or a temporary tax holiday
senses.definitionCN: 一次性决定，如刺激方案或临时减税期
senses.example: The discretionary part of fiscal policy was small compared with the automatic part.
senses.exampleCN: 财政政策中相机抉择的部分比起自动部分要小。
senses.why: the part that needs a vote is only the tip; most of the budget moves with the cycle on its own.
senses.whyCN: 需要表决的只是尖端，大部分预算随周期自行起落。

senses.title: Fiscal consolidation to restore the balance
senses.titleCN: 以财政整顿恢复收支平衡
senses.definition: a planned combination of tax rises and spending cuts to bring debt under control
senses.definitionCN: 为控制债务而计划实施的加税与减支组合
senses.example: Fiscal consolidation was delayed until recovery was secure.
senses.exampleCN: 财政整顿被推迟到复苏稳固之后。
senses.why: repair is not a single act but a programme stretched over years, which is why it has its own name.
senses.whyCN: 修补不是单一动作，而是拉长数年的方案，因此有自己的名字。

senses.title: A stimulus package as a single act
senses.titleCN: 作为单独立法的刺激方案
senses.definition: a named law or programme that spends or cuts taxes within a fixed period
senses.definitionCN: 在固定期限内支出或减税的具名法律或计划
senses.example: The stimulus package was the largest fiscal policy action since the war.
senses.exampleCN: 该刺激方案是战后最大的财政政策行动。
senses.why: a package bundles many measures under one vote, so the whole bundle is spoken of as one action.
senses.whyCN: 方案把许多措施捆在一次表决之下，整捆便被当作一个动作来说。

senses.title: Coordination with monetary policy
senses.definition: the setting of the budget in view of what the central bank is doing with rates
senses.definitionCN: 参照央行利率动作来设定预算
senses.example: Fiscal policy and monetary policy pulled in opposite directions for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 有一年，财政政策与货币政策朝相反方向用力。
senses.why: the two authorities act on the same demand, so their settings are always read against each other.
senses.whyCN: 两个当局作用于同一需求，因此彼此的设定总被相互对照。

intro.en: The phrase joins fiscal, from Latin fiscus 'money chest', with policy, from Greek politeia 'government' by way of Latin and French. It became standard in the twentieth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把来自拉丁 fiscus「钱箱」的 fiscal 与经拉丁语、法语上溯希腊 politeia「治理」的 policy 连在一起，20 世纪成为标准术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fiscus moved from a woven basket to the chest of the Roman treasury and then to the treasury as an institution.
items.cn: fiscus 从编织篮转为罗马国库的钱箱，再转为作为机构的国库。

items.en: Fiscalis meant 'of the treasury', and Old French fiscal brought it into English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: fiscalis 意为「国库的」，古法语 fiscal 于 16 世纪把它带入英语。

items.en: Politeia named citizenship and the running of a city; Latin politia and Old French policie carried it toward English policy.
items.cn: politeia 指公民身份与城邦治理；拉丁 politia 与古法语 policie 把它带向英语 policy。

items.en: Policy first meant a system of government, and only later any deliberate course of action chosen by an authority.
items.cn: policy 先指治理体系，后来才指权威选定的任何有意路线。

items.en: Fiscal policy became a standard term in the 1930s and 1940s, when governments took explicit responsibility for managing demand.
items.cn: 财政政策在 20 世纪 30 与 40 年代成为标准术语，当时政府明确承担管理总需求的职责。

items.en: Automatic stabilizers, consolidation and fiscal space were added as named parts of the same practice in the later twentieth century.
items.cn: 自动稳定器、财政整顿与财政空间在 20 世纪后期作为同一实践的有名部分被添入。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the chest or on government; group two holds policies and measures that are often compared with it.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「钱箱」或「治理」词根的词；第二组是常与之比较的政策与措施。

entries.definition: Relating to public money; the full phrase adds that a deliberate course is being followed.
entries.definitionCN: 指与公款有关；整个短语另含「正在遵循一条有意路线」。

entries.definition: In public-money terms; it describes how an action is done, not which policy it is.
entries.definitionCN: 指从公款角度；它描述动作方式，而非政策本身。

entries.definition: A settled course of action; alone it could concern health or trade rather than the budget.
entries.definitionCN: 指既定行动路线；单独使用时可以指卫生或贸易而非预算。

entries.definition: Of the body or of matter, from a Greek root; it shares only a sound with fiscal.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体或物质，出自希腊词根；与 fiscal 仅读音相近。

entries.definition: Central bank action through money and credit; fiscal policy acts through taxes and spending.
entries.definitionCN: 指央行通过货币与信贷行动；财政政策则通过税收与支出行动。

entries.definition: The annual plan of income and outgo; fiscal policy is the stance expressed through such plans.
entries.definitionCN: 指年度收支计划；财政政策是通过这类计划表达的立场。

entries.definition: Deliberate choices about who pays and how much; fiscal policy covers spending as well.
entries.definitionCN: 指关于谁缴、缴多少的有意选择；财政政策还包括支出。

entries.definition: A programme of cuts and tax rises to reduce debt; it is one setting of fiscal policy.
entries.definitionCN: 指以减支加税降低债务的方案；它只是财政政策的一种设定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real pieces of the compound, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词的真实成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The public chest plus a chosen course: how much goes in by tax and how much goes out by spending.
normal.cn: 公家钱箱加一条选定路线：收多少税进来，花多少钱出去。

normal.en: The family runs fiscal, fiscally, fisc, policy, policymaker, confiscate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括财政的、在财政上、国库、政策、政策制定者、没收。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: expansionary, contractionary, consolidation, fiscal space.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出设定：扩张性、紧缩性、整顿、财政空间。

normal.en: Automatic stabilizers work without a vote; discretionary measures need one.
normal.cn: 自动稳定器不经表决就起作用；相机抉择措施则需要表决。

normal.en: Two levers face each other: taxes and spending on one side, rates and money on the other.
normal.cn: 两根杠杆相对：一边是税收与支出，一边是利率与货币。

abstract.en: Picture one hand adding a tax line and another hand writing a road contract, on the same ledger.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在账簿上加一行税，另一只手在同一本账簿上写公路合同。

abstract.en: Picture a thermostat that warms the room when the outside turns cold, without anyone touching it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只恒温器，屋外变冷时它自己加热房间，无人触碰。

abstract.en: Picture a family that spends more in a hard year and must repay afterwards.
abstract.cn: 想象一户人家在艰难之年多花钱，之后必须补回来。

examples.en: Fiscal policy was the main tool left once interest rates reached zero.
examples.cn: 利率触零之后，财政政策成了剩下的主要工具。

examples.en: A credible fiscal policy can lower borrowing costs even before it is enacted.
examples.cn: 可信的财政政策甚至在立法之前就能降低借款成本。

examples.en: The two policies clashed: tight fiscal policy and easy monetary policy at the same time.
examples.cn: 两项政策相互冲突：财政政策紧缩的同时货币政策宽松。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「财政的」加「政策」——政府一手加税、一手花钱，用这本账簿调节经济 → 财政政策

root: fiscal 来自拉丁 fiscus「钱箱、国库」及其形容词 fiscalis；policy 经拉丁 politia、古法语 policie 上溯希腊 politeia「公民身份、治理」，根为 polis「城邦」。复合术语在 20 世纪 30 至 40 年代定型。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses are one ledger held in different ways: the overall stance, the two directions of opening or closing the chest, the parts that move by themselves, the parts voted on, the repair of the balance, a single stimulus act, and the argument with the central bank.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一本账簿的八种拿法：总立场、开箱与关箱的两个方向、自己会动的部分、需要表决的部分、修补差额、单独立法的刺激行动，以及与央行的争论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands on one ledger, one adding a tax line, one writing a public works contract.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手在同一本账簿上，一只加税行，一只写公共工程合同。

branches.en: STANCE AND OPENING: the general course, and the deliberate widening of the deficit.
branches.cn: 立场与开箱：总路线，以及有意扩大赤字。

branches.en: CLOSING AND REPAIR: austerity closes the chest, consolidation plans the repair.
branches.cn: 关箱与修补：紧缩关上钱箱，整顿计划修补。

branches.en: SELF-MOVING PARTS: benefits and taxes that respond to the cycle without a new law.
branches.cn: 自己会动的部分：无需新立法即随周期反应的救济与税收。

branches.en: THE VOTED ACT: discretionary measures, and a named package as one large action.
branches.cn: 经表决的行动：相机抉择措施，以及作为单一大动作的具名方案。

branches.en: TWO LEVERS: the budget must be set with the central bank's rates in view.
branches.cn: 两根杠杆：设定预算时必须考虑央行的利率。

intro.en: The phrase is a Latin-derived adjective for the public chest plus a Greek-derived noun for a governing course.
intro.cn: 这个短语是一个表示公家钱箱的拉丁系形容词，加一个表示治理路线的希腊系名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fiscus and fiscalis supply the first half; Latin politia, from Greek politeia, supplies the second.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fiscus 与 fiscalis 提供前半；拉丁 politia（源自希腊 politeia）提供后半。

items.exampleCN: 这项措施在财政上是中性的。
政策制定者权衡了成本。

items.example: The polity is small but stable.
items.exampleCN: 这个政治共同体虽小却稳定。

definition_zh: 有浮力的；能漂浮的；轻快的；乐观的；（市场）保持景气的
definition_en: able to float or keep something afloat; also light-hearted, cheerful or economically firm
core_image: 一块干木被按进水里，手一松就立刻弹回水面，还带着水珠
scene: 一块干木被按进水里，松手后立刻弹回水面。 Dry wood is buoyant enough to float for days.
sceneCN: 这里 buoyant 指「具有浮力、能漂浮的」（第 1 个义项：物理上的浮性）；句意为干木的浮力足以使它漂浮数日。

pos.zh: 有浮力的；能漂浮的；轻快的；乐观的；保持景气的

derivatives.zh: buoy + -ancy（拉丁 -antia 抽象名词后缀）→ 浮力；浮性；乐观
buoyant + -ly（副词后缀）→ 轻快地；乐观地
buoy（中古荷兰语 boeye「浮标」）→ 使浮起、鼓舞；浮标
buoyant + plume（羽流）→ 上升羽流：因密度较小而上升的流体柱
buoyant + force（力）→ 浮力：流体对物体的向上作用力

senses.title: Able to float
senses.definition: able to stay on the surface of a liquid
senses.definitionCN: 能留在液体表面而不下沉
senses.example: Dry wood is buoyant enough to float for days.
senses.exampleCN: 干木的浮力足以使它漂浮数日。
senses.why: a thing is buoyant when the fluid pushes up at least as hard as gravity pulls down.
senses.whyCN: 当流体向上推的力至少等于重力向下拉时，物体就是有浮力的。

senses.title: Keeping something afloat
senses.titleCN: 能托住他物的：提供浮力
senses.definition: having enough lift to support a load
senses.definitionCN: 有足够托举力承载负荷
senses.example: The hull is buoyant even with a full cargo.
senses.exampleCN: 船体即使满载货物也有浮力。
senses.why: the adjective can describe not only the floater but also the thing whose lift keeps another object up.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词不仅能描述漂浮者，也能描述以其托举力撑住他物的东西。

senses.title: Rising through a fluid
senses.definition: less dense than the surrounding fluid and therefore rising
senses.definitionCN: 密度小于周围流体因而上升
senses.example: A buoyant plume rises from the vent.
senses.exampleCN: 一股上升羽流从喷口升起。
senses.why: the same density rule that floats a boat lifts a warm plume through colder water.
senses.whyCN: 托起船只的密度规则，同样把暖羽流举过更冷的水。

senses.title: Light-hearted
senses.definition: cheerful and lively in mood
senses.definitionCN: 情绪愉快而活泼
senses.example: The children were buoyant after the race.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛之后孩子们情绪高涨。
senses.why: mood is described with up-down images, and what floats stays up; hence the cheerful sense.
senses.whyCN: 心情用上下意象描述，而浮得起的东西留在上面，于是产生愉快义。

senses.title: Optimistic and resilient
senses.definition: able to recover confidence after difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 困难之后能恢复信心
senses.example: She remained buoyant despite the rejection.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管遭到拒绝，她仍然乐观。
senses.why: coming back to the surface after being pushed down is the physical shape of recovering optimism.
senses.whyCN: 被压下去后回到水面，正是恢复乐观的物理形状。

senses.title: Firm in market terms
senses.definition: active and strong, said of prices, demand or an economy
senses.definitionCN: 指价格、需求或经济活跃而强劲
senses.example: The housing market remained buoyant through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 住房市场在整个冬季保持景气。
senses.why: prices that do not sink are described as floating high, which is the economic use of the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 不下沉的价格被描述为浮得高，这就是这个形容词的经济用法。

senses.title: Confident in manner
senses.definition: showing easy confidence and high spirits
senses.definitionCN: 表现出从容的自信与高涨的情绪
senses.example: He gave a buoyant wave from the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 他在台上轻快地挥手。
senses.why: the mood sense extends from feeling to visible behaviour, which is how the adjective describes a manner.
senses.whyCN: 情绪义从感受延伸到可见行为，这个形容词因此也能描述举止。

senses.title: Lifting the atmosphere
senses.definition: making a place or event feel cheerful
senses.definitionCN: 使场所或事件显得愉快
senses.example: The music gave the room a buoyant atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐给房间带来轻快的气氛。
senses.why: what lifts people's spirits is said to lift the atmosphere itself.
senses.whyCN: 能把人的情绪托起来的东西，也被说成托起了气氛本身。

intro.en: Buoyant is formed in English from buoy plus the Latin-derived adjective suffix -ant, from -antem. The origin of buoy is unsettled; a link to Latin boia 'leather collar' is a hypothesis only. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: buoyant 在英语中由 buoy 加拉丁语源形容词后缀 -ant（来自 -antem）构成。buoy 的来源没有定论，与拉丁 boia「皮制颈环」的联系仅是假说。年代均为约数。

items.en: Buoy came into English in the sixteenth century, probably from Middle Dutch boeye or Old French buie, a float or fetter.
items.cn: buoy 于十六世纪进入英语，可能来自中古荷兰语 boeye 或古法语 buie，指浮标或束缚物。

items.en: Source uncertain: no agreed pre-English source exists, and the Latin boia suggestion remains unproven.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语之前的来源没有共识，拉丁 boia 的说法未获证明。

items.en: The suffix -ant comes from Latin -antem, the present participle ending used in adjectives such as buoyant and defiant.
items.cn: 后缀 -ant 来自拉丁 -antem，即现在分词词尾，用于 buoyant、defiant 这类形容词。

items.en: The adjective appears in the early eighteenth century for objects that float.
items.cn: 这个形容词于十八世纪初出现，用于会漂浮的物体。

items.en: By the nineteenth century buoyant described spirits and markets as well as hulls.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，buoyant 除船体之外也描述情绪与市场。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the earliest citation differs across dictionaries, though the derivation is clear.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：各家词典所给最早书证不同，尽管派生关系清楚。

note.en: Group one holds the adjectives most often confused with buoyant; group two holds the mood and market words with overlapping meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是常与 buoyant 混淆的形容词；第二组是语义重叠的情绪与市场词。

entries.definition: The force or quality itself; buoyant is the adjective describing a thing that has it.
entries.definitionCN: 指力或性质本身；buoyant 是描述具有该性质的形容词。

entries.definition: Able to be floated or transported on water; it is about capability, not the upward force.
entries.definitionCN: 能够漂浮或被水上运输的；说的是能力，不是向上力量。

entries.definition: Resting on the surface now; buoyant says the object can do so, not that it is doing so.
entries.definitionCN: 此刻停在表面；buoyant 说物体能做到，而非正在做。

entries.definition: Covered by water; it is the opposite of floating at the surface.
entries.definitionCN: 被水覆盖；与浮在水面相对。

entries.definition: Happy and pleasant in mood; buoyant adds energy and the image of rising.
entries.definitionCN: 心情愉快和悦；buoyant 更带活力与上升的意象。

entries.definition: Expecting good outcomes; buoyant stresses resilience and lifted spirits rather than prediction.
entries.definitionCN: 预期好结果；buoyant 强调韧性与情绪高涨，而非预测。

entries.definition: Able to recover quickly from difficulty; it is close to the emotional sense of buoyant but less about mood.
entries.definitionCN: 能从困难中迅速恢复；接近 buoyant 的情绪义，但较少涉及心情。

entries.definition: Powerful or firm, used of markets; buoyant is more specific and suggests upward activity.
entries.definitionCN: 强劲有力，可用于市场；buoyant 更具体，暗示向上的活跃。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real physics, real markets and real morphology, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的物理、真实的市场与真实的构词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: buoyant is the adjective of buoyancy: if buoyancy is the push, buoyant is what the push can hold up.
normal.cn: buoyant 是 buoyancy 的形容词：浮力是推力，buoyant 是这股推力托得住的东西。

normal.en: -ant is a present-participle ending, like in defiant: a thing in the act of staying up.
normal.cn: -ant 是现在分词词尾，如 defiant：一个正保持在上面的东西。

normal.en: Three uses in one word: a hull, a mood, a market.
normal.cn: 一个词三种用法：船体、心情、市场。

normal.en: Warm fluid is buoyant because it is lighter than what surrounds it.
normal.cn: 暖流体有浮力，因为它比周围的东西轻。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: buoyant mood, buoyant market, buoyant plume.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：轻快心情、景气市场、上升羽流。

abstract.en: Buoyant is the refusal to stay at the bottom.
abstract.cn: buoyant 是拒绝留在底部的态度。

abstract.en: A buoyant mood is a private life jacket.
abstract.cn: 轻快的心情是一件私人救生衣。

abstract.en: Prices can float, and so can people.
abstract.cn: 价格能浮，人也能浮。

examples.en: Cork is buoyant because it is mostly trapped air.
examples.cn: 软木有浮力，因为它大部分是封住的空气。

examples.en: The team stayed buoyant after the first defeat.
examples.cn: 首场失利后，这支队伍仍然乐观。

examples.en: Buoyant demand pushed prices higher.
examples.cn: 旺盛的需求把价格推高。

dict_mnemonic.text: buoy（浮标）+ -ant（性质）＝能浮的；物理上浮得起，心情上轻快，市场上坚挺，三义同源。

root: buoy（中古荷兰语 boeye 或古法语 buie「浮标、束缚物」，更早来源不确定）+ 拉丁现在分词词尾 -antem → -ant；十八世纪初出现。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one floating quality: a thing that floats, a thing that holds others up, a fluid that rises, a light mood, resilience, a firm market, confident manner and an uplifting atmosphere.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种漂浮性质展开：会浮的物、能托住他物的物、会上升的流体、轻快心情、韧性、坚挺市场、自信举止与上扬的气氛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plank pressed under water springs back to the surface when released.
core.cn: 核心意象：木板被按入水下，一松手就弹回水面。

branches.en: FLOAT AND SUPPORT: the object floats, and the object can hold another up.
branches.cn: 漂浮与支撑：物体自己浮，物体也能托住另一个。

branches.en: CONVECTION: lightness makes a plume climb.
branches.cn: 对流：轻使羽流上升。

branches.en: MOOD: lightness of feeling and recovery after pressure.
branches.cn: 心情：感受的轻快与受压后的恢复。

branches.en: MARKET: prices that stay high and active.
branches.cn: 市场：保持高位与活跃的价格。

branches.en: VISIBLE CHEER: confident manner and a lifted atmosphere.
branches.cn: 可见的愉悦：自信举止与上扬的气氛。

intro.en: Buoyant is a borrowed noun stem plus a Latin participial suffix, so the derivation is fully readable.
intro.cn: buoyant 是借入名词词干加拉丁分词后缀，派生关系完全可读。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -antem is the Latin entry. Buoy has no established Latin ancestor, so no Latin noun is listed for it.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀 -antem 是拉丁条目。buoy 没有已确立的拉丁祖先，因此不列其拉丁名词。

items.example: The ending also shapes defiant and pleasant.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾也构成 defiant 与 pleasant。

items.example: Buoyant and tolerant share the ending.
items.exampleCN: buoyant 与 tolerant 共用这个词尾。

items.meaning: the force or quality of floating

items.meaningCN: 轻快地；带着上扬劲儿地

items.example: The buoyant plume reached the thermocline.

items.meaning: the upward force of a fluid
items.example: The buoyant force equals displaced weight.
items.exampleCN: 浮力等于排开流体的重量。

items.example: Children wear buoyancy aids on the lake.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们在湖上穿助浮衣。

definition_zh: 借方；借方分录；记入借方；扣款；借记卡支付
definition_en: an entry recording money paid out or charged, the left-hand side of a ledger, or to charge an account
core_image: 收银台的小屏幕上跳出一笔扣款，账本左侧多了一行数字
scene: 收银台前，顾客把卡片插入机器，输入密码，屏幕上跳出一笔扣款。 The clerk recorded the debit against the customer's account.
sceneCN: 这里 debit 指「借方分录、扣款」（第 1 个义项：记录资金被付出的那一笔账）；句意为职员把这笔扣款记在客户的账户上。图中可辨识物件：刷卡机、密码键盘、屏幕数字、账本左栏。

pos.zh: 借方；借方分录；扣款（可数）

derivatives.zh: 债务（同源双重借词）
债务人
债券
借记卡
直接扣款

senses.title: An entry for money paid out
senses.definition: a bookkeeping entry that records money leaving an account or being charged to it
senses.definitionCN: 记录资金离开某账户或被计入其支出的记账条目
senses.example: The clerk recorded the debit against the customer's account.
senses.exampleCN: 职员把这笔扣款记在客户的账户上。
senses.why: debit comes from the Latin word for what is owed, and bookkeeping turned it into the entry that records a claim against an account.
senses.whyCN: debit 来自拉丁语表示「被欠之物」的词，记账把它变成了记录对某账户的债权要求的条目。

senses.title: The left-hand side of a ledger
senses.definition: the left side of a double-entry account, where increases in assets and decreases in liabilities are entered
senses.definitionCN: 复式账户的左侧，登记资产增加与负债减少
senses.example: Every debit on the left must have a credit on the right.
senses.exampleCN: 左侧的每一笔借方都必须在右侧有一笔贷方。
senses.why: double-entry bookkeeping fixed debit to the left by convention, so the word also names that side of the page.
senses.whyCN: 复式记账按惯例把借方固定在左侧，因此这个词也指页面的那一侧。

senses.title: To charge an account
senses.definition: to take a sum out of an account by recording it as an amount owed or paid
senses.definitionCN: 把一笔金额记为应付或已付，从而从账户中扣除
senses.example: The bank debited the fee at the end of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 银行在月末扣除了这笔手续费。
senses.why: the noun became a verb meaning to make a debit entry, that is, to place a charge against an account.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词，意为做一笔借方分录，也就是对账户施加一笔扣款。

senses.title: The amount charged
senses.definition: the sum recorded in one debit entry
senses.definitionCN: 一笔借方分录所记录的金额
senses.example: The monthly debit for the gym is small.
senses.exampleCN: 健身房每月扣款金额不大。
senses.why: as with many action nouns, the entry and the sum it carries are both called a debit.
senses.whyCN: 与许多动作名词一样，分录与它所载的金额都被称为 debit。

senses.title: A debit card payment
senses.definition: a payment made by card that takes money directly from a current account
senses.definitionCN: 用卡片直接从活期账户扣钱的支付方式
senses.example: She paid by debit at the counter.
senses.exampleCN: 她在柜台用借记卡付款。
senses.why: a debit card is named for the immediate debit it creates, unlike a credit card which lends for a while.
senses.whyCN: 借记卡因即时产生扣款而得名，与先借后还的信用卡相对。

senses.title: An accounting effect
senses.definition: in accounting, an entry that increases assets or expenses and decreases liabilities or equity
senses.definitionCN: 会计上使资产或费用增加、负债或权益减少的条目
senses.example: The purchase was a debit to the equipment account.
senses.exampleCN: 这次采购是设备账户的一笔借方。
senses.why: the left-side rule defines debit by its effect on each class of account, not by whether it feels like a loss.
senses.whyCN: 左侧规则按对各账户类别的影响来定义借方，而不是按它感觉是否像损失。

senses.title: A burden charged against something
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：记在某物账上的负担
senses.definition: figuratively, something recorded as a disadvantage or cost against a person or plan
senses.definitionCN: 比喻上指被记为某人或某计划的一项不利或代价
senses.example: The delay was a debit against the project's reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误是记在项目声誉上的一笔负账。
senses.why: the ledger metaphor lets any cost or fault be entered on the debit side of a reputation.
senses.whyCN: 账簿比喻让任何代价或过失都能被记入声誉的借方。

senses.title: A thing owed, in older use
senses.definition: historically, a debt or an amount owed, before the word became specialised in bookkeeping
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指债务或所欠金额，在词义专门化为记账术语之前
senses.example: The old ledger lists each debit beside the name of its owner.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧账簿把每一笔欠款列在债主名字旁边。
senses.why: the accounting sense grew out of the older sense of an amount owed, which survives in the wording of old accounts.
senses.whyCN: 记账义由「所欠金额」的旧义生长而来，旧式账目用语中仍可见其痕迹。

intro.en: Debit is Latin debitum borrowed directly into English, while debt is the same Latin word filtered through French. They are doublets. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: debit 是直接借入英语的拉丁 debitum，而 debt 是同一个拉丁词经法语过滤后的形式。二者是双重借词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Debere 'to owe' was built on de- 'away from' plus habere 'to have': to have what belongs to another.
items.cn: debere「欠」由 de-「离开」加 habere「有」构成：持有属于他人之物。

items.en: Its neuter past participle debitum meant 'that which is owed' and served as a noun in accounts and law.
items.cn: 其中性过去分词 debitum 意为「被欠之物」，在账务与法律中作名词使用。

items.en: Debt came through Old French dette, losing and later restoring the b; debit was taken straight from Latin in the fifteenth century, keeping the b.
items.cn: debt 经古法语 dette 而来，b 先丢失后又被补回；debit 于 15 世纪直接从拉丁语借入，保留了 b。

items.en: As double-entry bookkeeping spread, debit was fixed to the left side of an account, and credit to the right.
items.cn: 随着复式记账普及，debit 被固定在账户左侧，credit 在右侧。

items.en: In the late twentieth century the debit card took the name because it debits an account at once rather than lending.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期，借记卡取用这个名字，因为它即刻扣减账户，而非提供借款。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact date of the accounting sense is not settled, and the pre-Latin origin of habere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：会计义的确切年代没有定论，habere 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same Latin word or close in shape; group two holds accounting and money-movement terms that are easily mixed with debit.
note.cn: 第一组是同出那个拉丁词或字形相近的形式；第二组是易与 debit 混淆的记账与资金流词。

entries.definition: The same Latin source through French; debt is the obligation, debit is the ledger entry that records it.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁来源经法语而来；debt 是义务，debit 是记录它的分录。

entries.definition: The party who owes; debit is an accounting entry, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 欠债的一方；debit 是会计条目，不是人。

entries.definition: A written acknowledgement of a debt; it looks close but names a security, not an entry.
entries.definitionCN: 承认债务的书面凭证；字形相近，但指证券而非分录。

entries.definition: A card that debits a current account at once; the word debit alone does not mean the card.
entries.definitionCN: 即时扣减活期账户的卡；单说 debit 并不指这张卡。

entries.definition: The right-hand entry in double-entry bookkeeping, and also the trust that allows deferred payment.
entries.definitionCN: 复式记账中右侧的条目，也指允许延期付款的信任。

entries.definition: To ask for payment or put a cost on an account; debit is its bookkeeping counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 要求付款或把费用记在某账上；debit 是它的记账对应词。

entries.definition: Cash removed by the customer; a debit is the record of it, and also covers card payments.
entries.definitionCN: 客户取出的现金；debit 是它的记录，也涵盖刷卡支付。

entries.definition: Any single written item in a ledger; a debit is one kind of entry.
entries.definitionCN: 账簿中任何单独一条书写项；debit 是其中一种条目。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'away' + habere 'have': what is owed has gone away from its owner, and the entry records the gap.
normal.cn: de-「离开」+ habere「有」：被欠之物离开了主人，分录记录这个缺口。

normal.en: The family runs debit, debt, debtor, debenture, debit card and direct debit.
normal.cn: 同族包括 debit、debt、debtor、debenture、debit card 与 direct debit。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: a debit entry, the debit side, debit and credit, a direct debit.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：借方分录、借方一侧、借贷双方、直接扣款。

normal.en: In double entry, debit is simply the left side; it is not a synonym for loss.
normal.cn: 在复式记账中，debit 就是左侧，并非「损失」的同义词。

normal.en: Debit and debt come from one Latin word by two different routes.
normal.cn: debit 与 debt 经由两条不同路径来自同一个拉丁词。

abstract.en: Picture a left-hand column that never quite balances with the right.
abstract.cn: 想象左侧一栏与右侧始终差一点才配平。

abstract.en: Picture a card that takes coins out of a pocket the moment it is swiped.
abstract.cn: 想象一张卡，一刷就从口袋里拿走硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a reputation with a debit column of its own.
abstract.cn: 想象一份声誉也有自己的借方栏。

examples.en: The bank debited the account for the annual fee.
examples.cn: 银行为年费从该账户扣款。

examples.en: Debits and credits must balance at the end of the day.
examples.cn: 日终时借贷双方必须配平。

examples.en: He paid with a debit card rather than a credit card.
examples.cn: 他用借记卡而不是信用卡付款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「debit 读作 deb-it」——账本左边记下付出的一笔 → 借方、扣款

root: 拉丁 debere「欠」= de-（离开）+ habere「有」，过去分词 debitum「被欠之物」直接借入英语；与经古法语而来的 debt 为同源双重借词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one entry: a value is recorded as taken away, and the same word covers the line in the book, the left side, the act of charging, the amount, a card payment, the accounting effect, a figurative cost and the old sense of a sum owed.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条分录展开：一笔价值被记为被取走，同一个词涵盖簿中那一行、左侧、扣款动作、金额、刷卡支付、会计影响、比喻代价，以及旧时「所欠金额」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a new line on the left of a ledger and a matching deduction on a small screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：账簿左侧新添一行，小屏幕上同时出现一笔扣减。

branches.en: THE ENTRY AND THE OLD DEBT: the line in the book grew out of the older sense of a sum owed.
branches.cn: 分录与旧债：簿中那一行由更早的「所欠金额」义生长而来。

branches.en: THE LEFT SIDE: convention and accounting effect define debit by position and by class of account.
branches.cn: 左侧：惯例与会计影响按位置和账户类别定义借方。

branches.en: THE CHARGE AND ITS AMOUNT: the act of charging and the sum charged share one noun.
branches.cn: 扣款与金额：扣款动作与所扣金额共用一个名词。

branches.en: THE CARD: a debit card is named for the immediate deduction it creates.
branches.cn: 卡片：借记卡因它造成的即时扣减而得名。

branches.en: A COST ON A REPUTATION: the ledger metaphor charges any fault to a person or a plan.
branches.cn: 声誉上的代价：账簿比喻把任何过失记到某人或某计划账上。

intro.en: Debit is a Latin participle borrowed whole, so its parts are a prefix, a verb of having and a participial ending, with no English ending added.
intro.cn: debit 是整词借入的拉丁分词，其成分是一个前缀、一个表示「有」的动词与一个分词词尾，没有再加英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere and debere give debit, debt and debtor, while debitum supplies both the English accounting term and its French-filtered doublet.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 habere 与 debere 衍生 debit、debt 与 debtor，debitum 同时提供英语会计术语与它经法语过滤的双重形式。

items.example: The prefix marks value going away from its owner.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记价值离开主人。

items.structure: habere, habui, habitum (Latin verb, second conjugation)
items.example: The root is the act of holding.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是持有的动作。

items.example: To owe is to hold another's property.
The participle became the accounting noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成了会计名词。

items.meaning: a charge recorded on the left
items.example: Each debit needs a matching credit.
items.exampleCN: 每一笔借方都需要对应的贷方。

items.example: The fee was debited at noon.
Debiting the account early avoids late fees.
items.exampleCN: 提前扣款可避免滞纳金。

items.meaning: a card that deducts at once
items.example: The debit card works without a credit line.
items.exampleCN: 借记卡无需信用额度即可使用。

items.example: Debt is the doublet of debit.
items.exampleCN: debt 是 debit 的同源双重形式。

definition_zh: 关键地；至关重要地；关键在于；决定性的是
definition_en: used to mark the one point on which the outcome depends, stronger and more specific than merely important
core_image: 十字路口只有一条路通向终点，路牌被红笔圈住，其余路口都暗下去
scene: 实验报告里有一处条件被红笔圈住，其余条件都划了淡线。 Crucially, the two groups were matched for age before the trial began.
sceneCN: 这里指点出决定成败的那一项条件（第 1 个义项：决定成败的关键点）；句意为关键在于，试验开始之前两组人的年龄已作过配对。场景要点：被红笔圈住的条件、暗下去的其余条件、只剩一条通向终点的路口。

pos.zh: 关键地；至关重要地；关键在于

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「十字」加形容词词尾构成，义为「关键的、决定性的」
由同一拉丁名词直接借入，义为「症结、关键点」
由十字名词加表示形状的词根构成，义为「十字形的」
由表示「钉上十字架、折磨」的拉丁动词构成，义为「使极度痛苦」
由折磨动词的现在分词加形容词词尾构成，义为「极痛苦的」

senses.title: The point on which the result turns
senses.definition: marks the condition or fact that decides how the whole comes out, raising it above the other points in the sentence
senses.definitionCN: 标出决定全局成败的条件或事实，把它抬到句中其他要点之上
senses.example: Crucially, the two groups were matched for age before the trial began.
senses.exampleCN: 关键在于，试验开始之前两组人的年龄已作过配对。
senses.why: Crux is a cross, and at a cross-roads the choice of one path decides the journey.
senses.whyCN: 十字路口的意思就是：站在岔口上，选哪条路决定整段行程。

senses.title: The formal sentence opener
senses.definition: placed first in academic or report prose to single out one point before the rest is read
senses.definitionCN: 置于学术或报告文字的开头，在读者读到其余内容之前先单挑出一点
senses.example: Crucially, the sample included no first-year students.
senses.exampleCN: 关键在于，样本里没有一年级学生。
senses.why: A paper has many claims, and the opener tells the reader which one carries the argument.
senses.whyCN: 一篇论文有很多说法，句首位置告诉读者哪一条承重。

senses.title: The parenthesis inside the clause
senses.definition: set between commas so that the decisive point is added without a change of sentence
senses.definitionCN: 用逗号夹在句中，把决定性的一点补进来而不另起一句
senses.example: The second condition, crucially, was never tested.
senses.exampleCN: 关键在于，第二个条件从未被检验。
senses.why: Insertion lets the writer mark the load-bearing point in a quieter voice.
senses.whyCN: 插入让作者用更轻的声音标出那处承重的地方。

senses.title: The weight placed at the end
senses.definition: in final position, where the decisive element is the last thing the reader is left with
senses.definitionCN: 处于句末，把决定性的成分留作读者最后握在手里的东西
senses.example: The choice of solvent mattered crucially.
senses.exampleCN: 溶剂的选择在要害上起了作用。
senses.why: What comes last in a sentence stays longest, so the end is where a decisive point can be planted.
senses.whyCN: 句子最后的东西留得最久，所以句末适合安放要害。

senses.title: A load-bearing premise
senses.definition: in reasoning, marks the premise or assumption that the whole argument stands on
senses.definitionCN: 在推理中标出整个论证所站立其上的前提或假设
senses.example: Crucially, the argument assumes that the two variables are independent.
senses.exampleCN: 关键在于，这个论证假定两个变量彼此独立。
senses.why: An argument falls if its load-bearing premise falls, and the word points to that premise.
senses.whyCN: 论证会随承重前提一起倒掉，这个词就指在那里。

senses.title: Harder than merely important
senses.definition: the boundary against importantly: that word gives weight, while this one says the outcome depends on the point
senses.definitionCN: 与「重要的是」的分界：那个词给出分量，这个词则说结果就系于这一点
senses.example: Importantly signals weight; crucially signals that the outcome depends on it.
senses.exampleCN: 「重要的是」给的是分量；这个词给的是「成败系于此」。
senses.why: Weight and dependence are different claims, and a writer who means the second needs the stronger word.
senses.whyCN: 有分量与成败所系是两种说法，想说后者的作者需要更硬的词。

senses.title: Not a statistical difference
senses.definition: the boundary against significantly: that word reports a measured difference, while this one reports a difference that decides the result
senses.definitionCN: 与「显著地」的分界：那个词报告测得的差别，这个词报告决定结果的差别
senses.example: Significantly reports a statistical difference; crucially reports a difference that decides the result.
senses.exampleCN: 「显著地」报告统计上的差别；这个词报告决定结果的差别。
senses.why: A measured difference need not be a decisive one: a result can be significant and still change nothing.
senses.whyCN: 测得的差别未必是决定性的差别：结果可以显著，却什么也没有改变。

senses.title: Emphasis in speech
senses.definition: in speech, often after and, a pointed reminder that the next detail is the one that matters
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中常跟在「而且」之后，提醒听者下面的细节才是最要紧的
senses.example: The door was locked and, crucially, nobody had a key.
senses.exampleCN: 门锁着，而且关键在于，谁也没有钥匙。
senses.why: Speech has no italics, so a word like this does the work of underlining.
senses.whyCN: 口语没有斜体，这样的词就干了划重点的活。

intro.en: Crucially is crucial plus -ly. Crucial was formed in English on Latin crux, crucis, a cross, and first described what belonged to a cross. The modern sense of decisive comes from the experimentum crucis, the cross-roads experiment that decides which of two paths is right.
intro.cn: 这个词由形容词加副词词尾构成。形容词是英语在拉丁语 crux、crucis「十字」上造出来的，最初指「与十字有关的」。今天「决定性」的意思来自 experimentum crucis，即那个决定两条路哪条正确的「十字路口实验」。

items.en: Crux meant a cross, and also a hard knot or turning point that has to be decided.
items.cn: 这个词指十字架，也指必须作出决断的症结或转折点。

items.en: The verb meant to put someone on a cross, and so to torment; cruciatus named the torment.
items.cn: 这个动词意为把人钉上十字架，因而指折磨；名词 cruciatus 指那种痛苦。

items.en: English formed the adjective with -al, at first in the literal sense of a cross; the date of that first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语加形容词词尾构成这个词，最初是「十字的」字面义；该首见年代不确定。

items.en: Bacon described a decisive test as a cross-roads experiment, instantia crucis; later writers called it experimentum crucis, the experiment that decides.
items.cn: 培根把决定性的检验称作「十字路口实验」，即 instantia crucis；后来的作者称之为 experimentum crucis，即「判决性实验」。

items.en: From that deciding experiment the adjective took its sense of decisive, and the adverb followed.
items.cn: 形容词从这种决定性的实验取得「决定性」之义，副词随后而来。

items.en: Papers and reports use the adverb to flag the one point on which their conclusion depends; its first use as such is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 论文与报告用这个副词标出结论所系的那一点；它作此用法的首见年代只有约略说法。

note.en: The first group shares the cross; the second holds the emphasis words it is weighed against, and one word from an unrelated family.
note.cn: 第一组共享「十字」这一词根；第二组是拿来与它权衡的强调类词，另有一个来自无关词族的形近词。

entries.definition: Decisive for an outcome, and in older use, shaped like a cross.
entries.definitionCN: 指对结果有决定作用的，旧义指十字形的。

entries.definition: The central difficulty or the point on which everything turns.
entries.definitionCN: 指核心难题，或一切都系于其上的那一点。

entries.definition: Shaped like a cross.
entries.definitionCN: 指形状像十字的。

entries.definition: Extremely painful, from the torment of the cross.
entries.definitionCN: 指极度痛苦的，源自十字架之刑的折磨。

entries.definition: From Latin crudus, raw or bloody, not from crux; it means causing suffering, not decisive.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「生的、血淋淋的」而非「十字」；意为残忍的，不指决定性。

entries.definition: Marks a point as weighty, without claiming that the result depends on it.
entries.definitionCN: 标记一点有分量，但不声称结果系于它。

entries.definition: Reports a large or statistically measured difference.
entries.definitionCN: 报告幅度大或经统计测得的差别。

entries.definition: Can mean decisively, but also means in a judging or fault-finding way.
entries.definitionCN: 既可指决定性地，也指以评判或挑错的方式。

entries.definition: Marks what something is in its nature, not what decides its fate.
entries.definitionCN: 标记某物在本性上是什么，而不是什么决定它的结局。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the cross at the heart of the word, the real deciding experiment, and the load-bearing point in an argument.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个词心里的「十字」、真实的判决性实验，以及论证里的承重点。

normal.en: Crux is a cross, and at a cross-roads one path must be chosen.
normal.cn: 词根是「十字」，站在十字路口必须选一条路。

normal.en: Bacon's cross-roads experiment decided between two explanations, and the word kept that deciding force.
normal.cn: 培根的十字路口实验在两种解释之间作出裁决，这个词保留的就是那股裁决力。

normal.en: Crucial, crux and crucially share the cross: the knot, the decisive test, and the adverb that flags it.
normal.cn: 「关键的」「症结」「关键地」都带着十字：那个结、那场判决、以及标出它的副词。

normal.en: Importantly says this matters; crucially says the result depends on it.
normal.cn: 「重要的是」说这要紧；这个词说结果就系于它。

normal.en: If you could replace it with significantly, you probably want a different word.
normal.cn: 如果你能用「显著地」替换它，那多半该换一个词。

abstract.en: A cross-roads is not a busy place but a deciding place.
abstract.cn: 十字路口不是热闹之处，而是决断之处。

abstract.en: Every argument has one joint that carries the weight, and the word points at it.
abstract.cn: 每个论证都有一处承重的接缝，这个词就指在那里。

abstract.en: Calling a detail crucial is a claim about the whole, not about the detail.
abstract.cn: 把一个细节说成关键，是在对整体作判断，而不是在说那个细节。

examples.en: Crucially, the second experiment used the same temperature as the first.
examples.cn: 关键在于，第二次实验用了与第一次相同的温度。

examples.en: The repair was cheap and, crucially, it held for a full year.
examples.cn: 这次修理很便宜，而且关键在于，它整整撑了一年。

examples.en: Crucially, none of the samples had been exposed to light.
examples.cn: 关键在于，没有任何一份样本见过光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「克鲁舍利」——十字路口只有一条路通向结果：关键地

root: 拉丁语 crux、crucis「十字」→ 英语 crucial「与十字有关的、决定性的」（其「决定性」义出自培根的十字路口实验）→ 加副词词尾构成。直接来源清楚；作「决定性」义的年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses vary the target and the force of the emphasis: the deciding point, the formal opener, the parenthesis, the end position, a load-bearing premise, the boundary against a word of weight, the boundary against a statistical word, and spoken emphasis.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项改变的是「强调什么」与「强调多硬」：决定点、正式句首、句中插入、句末、承重前提、与「重要的是」的分界、与统计用词的分界、口语强调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: at a cross-roads one road leads to the end, and its sign is circled in red while the others dim.
core.cn: 核心意象：十字路口只有一条路通向终点，它的路牌被红笔圈住，其余路口暗下去。

branches.en: THE DECIDING POINT AND THE SPOKEN NUDGE: the one condition that matters, underlined in speech.
branches.cn: 决定点与口语提醒：最要紧的那一项条件，在口语里被划了重点。

branches.en: THE THREE POSITIONS: at the head of the sentence, inside it, or at its end.
branches.cn: 三个位置：句首、句中、句末。

branches.en: THE LOAD-BEARING PREMISE: the assumption the whole argument rests on.
branches.cn: 承重前提：整个论证所依靠的那个假设。

branches.en: THE HARDER CLAIM: weight is not the same as dependence on the outcome.
branches.cn: 更硬的断言：有分量不等于成败系于此。

branches.en: THE MEASURED DIFFERENCE: statistical significance is another thing altogether.
branches.cn: 测得的差别：统计上的显著完全是另一回事。

intro.en: Crucially is an English adjective built on a Latin noun for a cross, with an English adverb ending on top.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语在拉丁语的「十字」名词上造成的形容词，再套一层英语副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies crux, cruciare and cruciatus; English supplies crucial, cruciform and the endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 crux、cruciare 与 cruciatus；英语提供了 crucial、cruciform 与词尾。

items.example: The noun supplies both the shape and the idea of a decisive knot.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既提供十字的形状，也提供「症结」的意思。

items.example: The verb names the punishment of the cross.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指十字架上的刑罚。

items.example: The noun names the suffering the verb causes.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指动词所造成的痛苦。

items.example: English formed it with -al, and later gave it the deciding sense.
items.exampleCN: 英语加词尾造出它，后来才给了它「决定性」一义。

items.example: The word keeps the literal shape of the cross.
items.exampleCN: 这个词保留十字的字面形状。

items.example: It turns the noun into an adjective.
It forms the verb of tormenting.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「折磨」的动词。

items.example: It forms the adjective of extreme pain.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示极度痛苦的形容词。

items.example: It makes the adverb that flags the decisive point.
items.exampleCN: 它构成标出关键点的副词。

derivatives.zh: 由十字名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「决定性的」
由同一拉丁名词直接借入，义为「症结」
由十字名词加表示形状的词根构成，义为「十字形的」
由表示「钉上十字架」的拉丁动词构成，义为「使极度痛苦」
由折磨动词的现在分词加形容词词尾构成，义为「极痛苦的」

definition_zh: 自治市镇；（英）有议员席位的市镇；（纽约的）行政区
definition_en: a self-governing town, or one of the divisions of a city such as New York
core_image: 挂着自治市铜牌的古老镇公所
scene: 镇公所门前的铜牌擦得锃亮，宣告这座小镇的自治地位。 Five boroughs make up New York City.
sceneCN: 这里 borough 是「行政区」（第 2 个义项：大城市的区划单位）；句意是五个行政区组成了纽约市。

derivatives.zh: 苏格兰拼写变体，义为「自治市镇」
法律史用语，义为「幼子继承制」

senses.title: A self-governing town
senses.definition: a town with its own local government and charter
senses.definitionCN: 拥有自己的地方政府与特许状的城镇
senses.example: The borough elected its own mayor and council.
senses.exampleCN: 该自治市镇选出自己的市长与议会。
senses.why: Old English burg was a fortified place; a walled town kept the right to rule itself.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 burg 指设防之地，有城墙的镇便保有自治之权。

senses.title: A division of a large city
senses.definition: one of the official districts of a large city such as New York
senses.definitionCN: 纽约等大城市的法定区划
senses.example: Five boroughs make up New York City.
senses.exampleCN: 五个行政区组成了纽约市。
senses.why: The old self-ruling town became the named district of the modern metropolis.
senses.whyCN: 昔日的自治小镇化为现代都会的命名区划。

senses.title: A parliamentary constituency of old England
senses.definition: a town entitled to send members to Parliament
senses.definitionCN: 有权向议会派遣议员的市镇
senses.example: The borough returned two members to Parliament.

senses.title: A person who sorts
senses.definition: a person whose work is to arrange things into groups
senses.definitionCN: 以把事物分组为工作的人
senses.example: The classifier sorted the specimens by species.
senses.exampleCN: 分类员按物种把标本分开。
senses.why: The -er suffix is agentive here: a human doing the sorting. This is the plainest reading of the word, and the base from which the technical senses branch.
senses.whyCN: 此处 -er 是施事后缀：一个在做分拣的人。这是该词最朴素的读法，也是技术义分叉的基座。

senses.title: A sorting machine
senses.definition: a machine that separates items by size, weight, or quality
senses.definitionCN: 按大小、重量或品质分离物料的机器
senses.example: The air classifier removes fine dust from the crushed ore.
senses.exampleCN: 气流分选机从碎矿中除去细尘。
senses.why: Industry extends the agent to metal: the machine does what the worker did. The suffix -er covers instruments as easily as people, a common English pattern.
senses.whyCN: 工业把施事扩展到机器：机器做工人做过的事。后缀 -er 与人一样容易指工具，这是英语常见模式。

senses.title: A grammatical classifier
senses.definition: a word or morpheme that must accompany a noun and marks its class, like the Chinese measure word ben used for books
senses.definitionCN: 必须与名词连用并标记其类别的词或语素，如汉语中书的“本”
senses.example: Chinese uses the measure word zhang for flat objects.
senses.exampleCN: 汉语用类别词“张”来数扁平物体。
senses.why: Linguistics borrowed the sorting image: the classifier puts a noun into a class (long, flat, human) before it can be counted. English has no full system, which is why the term is learned as a foreign concept.
senses.whyCN: 语言学借用了分拣意象：类别词先把名词归入某类（长形、扁平、人类），然后才能计数。英语没有完整系统，故该术语是作为外来概念学习的。

senses.title: A sign-language classifier
senses.definition: a handshape in sign language that represents a class of objects or how they move
senses.definitionCN: 手语中代表某类物体或其运动方式的手形
senses.example: The signer used a vehicle classifier for the moving car.
senses.exampleCN: 手语者用车辆类别词表示移动的车。
senses.why: Sign linguistics extends the grammatical sense to gesture: the handshape itself carries the class. The classifier is not a word but a form that categorizes what the verb describes.
senses.whyCN: 手语语言学把语法义扩展到手势：手形本身承载类别。类别词不是词，而是给动词所述对象归类的形式。

senses.title: A machine-learning classifier
senses.definition: an algorithm that assigns a label to new data after training on examples
senses.definitionCN: 在样本上训练后为新数据分配标签的算法
senses.example: The classifier predicts whether an email is spam.
senses.exampleCN: 该分类器预测邮件是否为垃圾邮件。
senses.why: Computing keeps the agent slot but fills it with a model. The classifier has learned a boundary between classes; its output is a label, and its quality is measured by accuracy, not by understanding.
senses.whyCN: 计算保留施事位置，却用模型填充。分类器学到了类与类之间的边界；输出是标签，质量以准确率衡量，而非以理解衡量。

senses.title: A biological taxonomist
senses.definition: a scientist who assigns organisms to taxonomic groups
senses.definitionCN: 把生物归入分类群的科学家
senses.example: Early classifiers placed whales among fish.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的分类学者把鲸归入鱼类。
senses.why: Biology is where classification became a formal science. The classifier's judgements are hypotheses about relatedness, and they can be wrong, as the whale case shows.
senses.whyCN: 生物学是分类成为正式科学之处。分类者的判断是关于亲缘关系的假设，可能出错，鲸的例子即是。

senses.title: A library classifier
senses.definition: a librarian who assigns classification numbers to books
senses.definitionCN: 给书籍编分类号的图书馆员
senses.example: The classifier gave the atlas a shelf mark.
senses.exampleCN: 分类员给这本地图册编了排架号。
senses.why: Library work makes the word institutional: the classifier applies an existing scheme rather than inventing classes. The agent's skill lies in reading a book accurately enough to place it.
senses.whyCN: 图书馆工作使该词制度化：分类员应用既有体系，而非发明类别。其技能在于把书读得足够准，以便安放。

senses.title: A content filter
senses.titleCN: 内容过滤器；过滤分类器
senses.definition: a system that sorts messages or media into wanted and unwanted categories
senses.definitionCN: 把信息或媒体分为想要与不想要的系统
senses.example: The classifier flagged the comment as abusive.
senses.exampleCN: 该过滤器把这条评论标为辱骂。
senses.why: This is the applied face of sense 05: the boundary is put to work. The word hides the human decisions behind the labels, including the choice of what counts as abuse.
senses.whyCN: 这是第 5 义的应用面：边界被投入使用。该词掩盖了标签背后的人为决定，包括“什么算辱骂”的选择。

senses.title: A class label
senses.definition: a tag or feature that marks which class an item belongs to
senses.definitionCN: 标记某物属于哪一类的标签或特征
senses.example: Each record carries a classifier in its metadata.
senses.exampleCN: 每条记录在元数据中带有一个类别标记。
senses.why: The rarest sense shifts from the sorter to the mark left by sorting. It is the trace of the act, not the act itself, and it shows how far the -er suffix can drift from 'person who'.
senses.whyCN: 最罕见的义项从分拣者转到分拣留下的标记。它是动作的痕迹而非动作本身，显示 -er 后缀可以离“做此事的人”多远。

intro.en: Classifier is classify plus -er. Classify comes from French classifier, built on classe, from Latin classis 'a division or class of citizens' (also 'a fleet'). The second element is -ifier, from Latin -ificare, from facere 'to make': to make into a class. The origin of classis itself is uncertain; one suggestion links it to calare 'to summon', picturing a called-up body of citizens. The grammatical sense is a 20C linguistic borrowing of the sorting image.
intro.cn: classifier 是 classify 加 -er。classify 出自法语 classifier，基于 classe，源于拉丁 classis“公民的等级/类别”（也指“舰队”）。第二部分 -ifier 出自拉丁 -ificare，源自 facere“做”：使成为一类。classis 本身的来源存疑，一说与 calare“召集”有关，构拟“被召集的公民体”。语法义是二十世纪语言学对“分拣”意象的借用。

items.en: classis means 'a division or class of Roman citizens', and also 'a fleet'; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: classis 意为“罗马公民的一个等级/类别”，也指“舰队”；其更深来源存疑。

items.en: One suggestion connects classis with calare 'to summon', so a class is 'those called together'. This is plausible, not proven.
items.cn: 一说把 classis 与 calare“召集”联系起来，于是 class 是“被召集到一起的人”。此说合理，但未证实。

items.en: classicus 'of the first class' is derived from classis and later gives English classic and classical.
items.cn: classicus“头等的”由 classis 派生，后来给出英语 classic 与 classical。

items.en: French classifier joins classe with -ifier, from Latin -ificare 'to make', so 'to make into a class'.
items.cn: 法语 classifier 把 classe 与 -ifier 结合，后者出自拉丁 -ificare“使…”，即“使成为一类”。

items.en: English adopts classify in the 18C; the agent noun classifier follows with the ordinary -er suffix.
items.cn: 英语于十八世纪引入 classify；施事名词 classifier 随后以普通 -er 后缀构成。

items.en: Linguistics applies classifier to Chinese measure words and to sign-language handshapes, extending the sorting image to grammar.
items.cn: 二十世纪语言学把 classifier 用于汉语“本”这类词及手语手形，把分拣意象扩展到语法。

note.en: The first group is the classify family and its endings; the second is words for sorting, which differ in whether they name a person, a system, or a single act.
note.cn: 第一组是 classify 词族及词尾；第二组是“分类”相关词，差别在于指人、指系统还是指一次动作。

entries.definition: the act or system of putting things into classes.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物归类的动作或体系。

entries.definition: to arrange into groups according to shared features.
entries.definitionCN: 按共同特征分组。

entries.definition: able to be placed in a class.
entries.definitionCN: 可被归类的。

entries.definition: a scientist who names and groups organisms. It is the biological specialist of classifier.
entries.definitionCN: 给生物命名并分组的科学家。是 classifier 在生物学的专指。

entries.definition: a person or machine that separates items. It is more physical and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 分拣人或分拣机。更具体，少技术性。

entries.definition: a tag naming the class of something. It is the output of classification, not the agent.
entries.definitionCN: 标明类别的标签。是分类的输出，而非施事。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin classis 'class', facere 'make' via -ify, and the -er suffix that covers both people and machines.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁 classis“类别”、经 -ify 的 facere“做”，以及兼指人与机器的 -er 后缀。

normal.en: Classify = class + -ify, 'make into a class'; add -er and you have the maker of classes.
normal.cn: classify = class + -ify“使成类”；再加 -er，就得到“造类者”。

normal.en: The same -er makes 'worker' and 'printer'. That is why a classifier can be a person or a machine.
normal.cn: 同一个 -er 造出 worker 与 printer。故 classifier 可以是人，也可以是机器。

normal.en: In Chinese, the phrase for 'one book' needs the measure word ben; the classifier is the drawer the noun must go into before it can be counted.
normal.cn: 汉语“一本书”需要“本”；类别词是名词在计数前必须进入的抽屉。

normal.en: A spam filter is a classifier: it draws a line between two classes and puts each mail on one side.
normal.cn: 垃圾邮件过滤器就是分类器：在两类之间画一条线，把每封邮件放一边。

normal.en: classis also meant 'fleet'. A fleet is a class of ships, which is a useful picture of a group called together.
normal.cn: classis 也指“舰队”。舰队就是一类船，这是“被召集的一组”的好画面。

abstract.en: Classification is power: the one who draws the classes decides what counts as same and what counts as other.
abstract.cn: 分类即权力：画类的人决定什么算相同、什么算相异。

abstract.en: Every classifier, human or machine, encodes a prior decision about which differences matter.
abstract.cn: 每个分类者，无论人或机器，都编码了“哪些差异重要”的先在决定。

abstract.en: A label is the trace of a judgement; mistaking the trace for the thing is how categories harden into prejudice.
abstract.cn: 标签是判断的痕迹；把痕迹当作事物本身，类别就硬化为偏见。

examples.en: The classifier placed the new species in its own genus.
examples.cn: 分类者把新物种归入独立属。

examples.en: Chinese requires a classifier between a number and a noun.
examples.cn: 汉语在数词与名词之间需要类别词。

examples.en: The trained classifier reaches 94 percent accuracy.
examples.cn: 训练好的分类器达到百分之九十四的准确率。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of classifier: a person, a machine, a grammar word, a sign-language handshape, a learning algorithm, a taxonomist, a librarian, a content filter, and a class label. All of them draw or apply a line between classes.
sensesIntro.cn: classifier 的九个义项：人、机器、语法词、手语手形、学习算法、生物分类学者、图书分类员、内容过滤器、类别标签。它们都在类与类之间画线或应用已有的线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand placing each object into a labelled drawer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把每件东西放进贴有标签的抽屉。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a worker, a scientist, a librarian each applies a scheme of classes.
branches.cn: 人：工人、科学家、图书馆员各自应用一套类别体系。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: a separator does the sorting with air, weight, or mesh.
branches.cn: 机器：分选机用气流、重量或筛网完成分拣。

branches.en: THE MARKER: grammar and sign language put the class into the noun's companion.
branches.cn: 标记：语法与手语把类别放进名词的伴随成分。

branches.en: THE ALGORITHM: a trained boundary assigns labels and filters content.
branches.cn: 算法：训练出的边界分配标签并过滤内容。

branches.en: THE TRACE: the label left behind is the act of sorting turned into metadata.
branches.cn: 痕迹：留下的标签是分拣动作变成的元数据。

intro.en: Classifier is classify plus -er. Classify is class + -ify, from Latin classis and facere. The family includes classification, classificatory, and classifiable; the base also gives class, classic, and classical.
intro.cn: classifier 是 classify 加 -er。classify 是 class + -ify，出自拉丁 classis 与 facere。词族含 classification、classificatory、classifiable；词基还给出 class、classic、classical。

latinIntro.en: Latin classis 'division, class' combines with -ificare 'to make' to form classifiere in Medieval Latin and classifier in French. English adds -ation, -atory, and -able to the same stem. The root classis also yields classicus 'first class', hence classic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 classis“类别”与 -ificare“使…”结合，形成中世纪拉丁 classifiere 与法语 classifier。英语在同一词干上加 -ation、-atory、-able。词根 classis 还给出 classicus“头等的”，即 classic。

definition_zh: 社会组织；人群编组方式；正式团体；结社过程；社区结构；对群体事务的经营管理
definition_en: the way people are grouped into roles, bodies and networks, and the work of keeping that grouping running
core_image: 河滩上的人群按活儿分成几拨，抬石的、烧饭的、记账的各有人领头，每组都清楚自己与谁搭班。
scene: 河滩上的人群按活儿分成几拨，抬石的、烧饭的、记账的各有人领头，谁与谁搭班写得清楚。 The social organization of the camp gives every family a task and a partner.
sceneCN: 这里 social organization 指「一群人被编组成不同班组的方式」（第 1 个义项：按活儿把人分拨并配上负责人的编组方式）；句意为营地的社会组织给每个家庭分配了一项任务和一个搭档。可辨识物件：河滩、石堆、灶火、账簿、分组用的木牌。

pos.zh: 社会组织；人群编组；正式团体（可数，指某个具体组织体）

derivatives.zh: organum「工具、器官」+ -ize（动词后缀）→ 由「器官」转为「使各部分成为整体、组织起来」
organize + -ation（动作与结果后缀）→ 由「组织」的动作转为「组织、机构」
organization + -al（形容词后缀）→ 由「组织」转为「组织层面的」
organize + -er（施事后缀）→ 由动作转为「组织者、筹办人」
dis-（否定前缀）加 organized → 由「有组织的」转为「杂乱无章的」

senses.title: How people are grouped
senses.definition: the way a body of people is divided into groups, each with a task and a place
senses.definitionCN: 一群人被分成若干小组、每组各有任务与位置的方式
senses.example: The social organization of the camp gives every family a task and a partner.
senses.exampleCN: 营地的社会组织给每个家庭分配了一项任务和一个搭档。
senses.why: organization comes from organum, a tool or organ, and -ation, a making; grouping people is making them work as parts of one body.
senses.whyCN: organization 来自 organum「工具、器官」加 -ation「造成」，把人们编组就是使他们像一个身体的各部分那样运作。

senses.title: A network of roles and institutions
senses.definition: the connected set of roles, offices and institutions through which a community carries on its business
senses.definitionCN: 一个共同体借以办事的、相互连接的角色、职位与制度
senses.example: A fishing village keeps a social organization of skippers, net makers and fishmongers.
senses.exampleCN: 渔村维持着一套由船主、织网人与鱼贩构成的社会组织。
senses.why: once the parts are organs, each has a function, and the functions must be linked before the whole can work.
senses.whyCN: 一旦各部分被看作器官，每一部分就有功能，而功能必须先被连接起来，整体才能运作。

senses.title: A formal body with rules
senses.definition: a formally established body, such as a club, a union or a charity, with membership and rules
senses.definitionCN: 正式设立的团体，如俱乐部、工会或慈善会，有成员资格与规章
senses.example: The grain fund is a social organization with written rules and elected officers.
senses.exampleCN: 粮食基金是一个有成文规章和选举产生负责人的社会组织。
senses.why: the result noun -ation also names the thing made, so the arranging can harden into an institution that exists in its own right.
senses.whyCN: -ation 这个结果名词也指被造成之物，因此编组的动作可以硬化为一个自行存在的机构。

senses.title: The process of getting organized
senses.definition: the process by which people come together, divide duties and set up a working arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 人们聚合起来、分派职责并建立运作安排的过程
senses.example: Neighbours began the social organization of a fire watch after the first dry summer.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个干旱的夏天之后，邻里开始了防火巡查的结社筹备。
senses.why: the same noun covers the act and the outcome, so it can name the work of organizing as well as the body organized.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既指动作也指结果，因此它既能指组织的活儿，也能指被组织起来的团体。

senses.title: The structure of a community
senses.definition: the settled shape of a community, including its groups, their ranks and their usual dealings
senses.definitionCN: 一个社区稳定的形状，包括它的各组人、各自等级与惯常往来
senses.example: The social organization of the island still centres on the church and the boat shed.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的社会组织仍以教堂与船棚为中心。
senses.why: a community organized year after year settles into a shape, and that shape is what observers call its organization.
senses.whyCN: 一个社区年复一年地被组织，就会稳定成一种形状，观察者把这个形状称作它的组织。

senses.title: Managing the affairs of a group
senses.titleCN: 对群体事务的经营管理
senses.definition: the work of arranging and running the affairs of a group, from duties to records
senses.definitionCN: 安排并运转一个群体的事务，从职责分派到记录保存
senses.example: She took over the social organization of the relief depot for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 她接手了救济站整个冬天的组织管理工作。
senses.why: the verb organize means to put parts in order; applied to people, it becomes the daily management of their affairs.
senses.whyCN: 动词 organize 意为把各部分排好；用在人身上，它就成了对群体事务的日常管理。

senses.title: Coordinating people for one purpose
senses.definition: the coordination of people and resources toward a single stated aim
senses.definitionCN: 为单一既定目标而协调人员与资源
senses.example: The rescue required a social organization that could form in an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这次救援需要一种能在一小时内成形的人群协调。
senses.why: the organic image supplies the point: many parts acting as one body for one end.
senses.whyCN: 器官的意象提供了要点：许多部分为了一个目的而像一个身体那样行动。

senses.title: Abstractly, any arrangement of a group
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何群体的具体安排
senses.definition: any concrete arrangement by which a particular group of people is put in order
senses.definitionCN: 把某一群具体的人排定的任何安排
senses.example: The ants show a social organization that no one designed.
senses.exampleCN: 蚂蚁呈现出一种无人设计的群体安排。
senses.why: strip away institutions and only an arrangement of parts remains, so the phrase can describe a hive as easily as a town.
senses.whyCN: 抽掉制度之后只剩各部分的安排，因此这个短语既能描写蜂巢，也能描写城镇。

intro.en: Organization comes from Latin organum, from Greek organon 'tool, instrument, organ', plus the action suffix -ation; organize is the verb built on organ with -ize. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: organization 来自拉丁 organum，出自希腊 organon「工具、器具、器官」，再加动作后缀 -ation；organize 是在 organ 上加 -ize 构成的动词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Organon meant 'tool, instrument, and also organ of the body'. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and forms offered for a pre-Greek root are reconstructions.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具，也指身体器官」。其更深来源不确定，为它给出的前希腊词根形式属重构形式。

items.en: Latin borrowed organon as organum, keeping both the tool sense and the body sense; the word also came to name a musical instrument.
items.cn: 拉丁把 organon 借作 organum，同时保留「工具」与「身体器官」两义；这个词后来也指乐器。

items.en: English organ names a body part and, separately, a musical instrument; the older tool sense survives mainly inside derived words.
items.cn: 英语 organ 指身体器官，又另指乐器；较旧的「工具」义主要残存在派生词里。

items.en: Organize was formed on organ with -ize, 'to make into an organized whole'; the verb is modern and its earliest uses are not precisely dated.
items.cn: organize 是在 organ 上加 -ize 构成，意为「使成为有组织的整体」；这个动词属近代产物，最早用法没有确切年代。

items.en: The suffix -ation marks an action or its result, from Latin -atio; added to organize it yields organization, the act of arranging and the thing arranged.
items.cn: 后缀 -ation 出自拉丁 -atio，标记动作或其结果；加在 organize 上得出 organization，既指安排的动作，也指被安排成的东西。

items.en: Source uncertain: no agreed first citation is recorded for organization, and the step from 'organ of the body' to 'arranged group of people' has no single documented date.
items.cn: 来源不确定：organization 的最早书证并无定说；由「身体器官」到「被安排的人群」这一步，也没有单一可考的年代。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the organ stock that look close to the headword; group two holds terms for social arrangements that differ in scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 organ 词干、与词条形近的词；第二组是范围不同的社会安排术语。

entries.definition: The verb for putting parts or people in order; the phrase is the result noun, so it names the arrangement rather than the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指把部分或人排好序的动词；短语是结果名词，因此指安排而非动作。

entries.definition: A part of a living body, or a musical instrument; it is one part, while social organization is the arrangement of many parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指活体的一个器官，或一件乐器；它是单个部分，而 social organization 是许多部分的安排。

entries.definition: Built on organ with -ic, it means of living organs, or grown without chemicals, and also describes parts that grow together; it never names a group of people.
entries.definitionCN: 由 organ 加 -ic 构成，指活体器官的、无化学种植的，也形容各部分长在一起；它从不指一群人。

entries.definition: From organ plus -ism, it names a single living body; the shared root makes it look technical kin, but it is a creature, not an arrangement of people.
entries.definitionCN: 由 organ 加 -ism 构成，指单个活体；共同的词根使它看似同类术语，但它指生物，不指人的安排。

entries.definition: The overall frame of institutions and ranks; social organization is the grouping and running that happens inside that frame.
entries.definitionCN: 指制度与等级的总体框架；social organization 是发生在这个框架内部的编组与运作。

entries.definition: A single established body or practice, such as a court or a school; social organization can cover many such bodies and the links between them.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个确立的机构或做法，如法庭或学校；social organization 可涵盖许多这类机构及其间的联系。

entries.definition: A body of people who have joined for a purpose, usually a formal one; it is one kind of social organization, not the general notion.
entries.definitionCN: 指为某目的而联合的一群人，通常是正式团体；它只是社会组织的一种，而非一般概念。

entries.definition: The people who live together and share things; social organization describes how those people are arranged, not who they are.
entries.definitionCN: 指共同生活并共享事物的人们；social organization 描写这些人如何被安排，而不是他们是谁。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: organon 'tool, organ' plus -ation: many parts made to work as one body.
normal.cn: organon「工具、器官」加 -ation：许多部分被使得像一个身体那样运作。

normal.en: Organize is organ plus -ize: to put the parts in order.
normal.cn: organize 是 organ 加 -ize：把各部分排好。

normal.en: The family runs organ, organize, organization, organizational, organizer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 organ、organize、organization、organizational、organizer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the angle: formal social organization, the social organization of work.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出角度：正式社会组织、劳动的社会组织。

normal.en: Sociology contrasts it with social structure: the grouping versus the wider frame.
normal.cn: 社会学把它与社会结构对照：编组对更宽的框架。

abstract.en: Picture a hand with five fingers doing what one arm could never do alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手的五根手指做出单靠一条胳膊做不到的事。

abstract.en: Picture a kitchen where each cook owns one task and no one owns the meal.
abstract.cn: 想象一间厨房，每位厨子只管一道工序，没有人拥有整桌菜。

abstract.en: Picture an anthill that runs perfectly with no blueprint anywhere.
abstract.cn: 想象一座蚁丘，没有任何图纸却运转得井井有条。

examples.en: The social organization of the harvest shifts with each new irrigation canal.
examples.cn: 每一条新水渠都会改变收获时节的社会组织。

examples.en: A union is a social organization built to bargain rather than to farm.
examples.cn: 工会是为谈判而不是为耕种建立的社会组织。

examples.en: Researchers compared the social organization of two primate troops.
examples.cn: 研究者比较了两个灵长类群体的社会组织。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「social（社交的）+ organ（器官）+ ization（造成）」——把一群人接成像器官那样各司其职的整体 → 社会组织、编组方式

root: 希腊 organon「工具、器官」→ 拉丁 organum → 英语 organ；organ + -ize → organize，organize + -ation → organization。英语 social organization。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one making: people are divided into parts, the parts are linked by roles, the linking hardens into a body, the act and the body share one noun, the community settles into a shape, the shape is managed, it is aimed at one purpose, and finally any arrangement of a group is read under the same name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一次「造成」展开：人被分成部分，部分由角色连接，连接硬化成一个团体，动作与团体共用同一个名词，社区稳定成一种形状，这个形状被经营管理，被指向一个目的，最后任何群体的安排都用同一个名称来读。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many hands fitted together until they work like one body.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多只手被装配到一起，直到它们像一个身体那样运作。

branches.en: GROUPING AND BODY: dividing people into parts can end in a formal body with rules.
branches.cn: 编组与团体：把人分成部分，最终可以形成一个有规章的正式团体。

branches.en: NETWORK AND PROCESS: roles are linked into a net, and the linking is itself an activity.
branches.cn: 网络与过程：角色被连成一张网，而连接本身就是一项活动。

branches.en: SHAPE AND MANAGEMENT: a community settles into a shape, and that shape has to be run.
branches.cn: 形状与管理：社区稳定成一种形状，而这个形状必须被运作。

branches.en: ONE AIM: the organic image narrows to many parts acting for a single end.
branches.cn: 一个目的：器官意象收窄为许多部分为一个目标行动。

branches.en: ANY ARRANGEMENT: with institutions removed, a hive or a town fits the same word.
branches.cn: 任何安排：去掉制度之后，蜂巢与城镇都适用同一个词。

intro.en: Organization is a Greek noun carried into Latin, fitted with an English verb suffix and then a Latin action suffix; the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: organization 是一个传入拉丁语的希腊名词，先加英语动词后缀，再加拉丁动作后缀；整个词族可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon became Latin organum, English organ and the verb organize; -ation then turned the verb into organization.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 organon 变成拉丁 organum，再变成英语 organ 与动词 organize；-ation 随后把这个动词变成 organization。

items.example: The Greek noun covered both a craftsman's tool and a body part.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词既指工匠的工具，也指身体的一部分。

items.structure: organum, organi (Latin noun, neuter, second declension)
items.example: Latin carried the Greek word into western scholarship.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁把这个希腊词带入西方学术。

items.meaning: a body part; a musical instrument
items.example: The heart is an organ in the plain bodily sense.
items.exampleCN: 心脏是「器官」最朴素意义上的一个器官。

definition_zh: 成熟；成熟期；（金融票据、合同等的）到期；到期日
definition_en: the state of being fully developed; the point at which a financial instrument or contract falls due

sceneCN: 这里指果实发育完成（第 1 个义项：生理或发育意义上的成熟）；句意为直到果实完全成熟，果园才开始采摘。图中可辨识物件：果树、糖度计、记录板、采果篮。
