senses.title: Biological maturity
senses.definition: the stage at which an organism can reproduce and its body has finished growing
senses.definitionCN: 生物能够繁殖、身体完成生长的阶段
senses.example: The seals reach sexual maturity at about four years old.
senses.exampleCN: 这些海豹大约四岁达到性成熟。
senses.why: Development has a natural end point, and the word names the moment when growth and reproduction are both available.
senses.whyCN: 发育有天然的终点，这个词命名的正是生长与繁殖都已具备的时刻。

senses.title: Emotional and judgemental maturity
senses.definition: the capacity to weigh consequences and act responsibly rather than impulsively
senses.definitionCN: 能权衡后果、负责任地行动而不凭冲动的能力
senses.example: The negotiations demanded patience and a certain maturity from both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判要求双方都有耐心与一定的成熟度。
senses.why: The same word for ripening is applied to character, because both describe something that has stopped being unripe.
senses.whyCN: 表示「成熟」的同一个词被用到性格上，因为两者都描述某物不再青涩。

senses.title: Ripeness of fruit or crops
senses.definition: the point at which a crop is ready to harvest, judged by colour, sugar or texture
senses.definitionCN: 作物达到可采收的程度，常以颜色、糖度或质地判断
senses.example: Growers test sugar levels to decide when the grapes reach maturity.
senses.exampleCN: 种植者测试糖度来决定葡萄何时成熟。
senses.why: Harvest timing needs a threshold, and the word names the stage where the fruit is fully formed and ready.
senses.whyCN: 采收时机需要一个阈值，这个词命名的就是果实完全成形且可用的阶段。

senses.title: A financial instrument falling due
senses.definition: the date on which a bond, note or loan must be repaid, or the state of having reached that date
senses.definitionCN: 债券、票据或贷款必须偿还的日期，或已到达该日期的状态
senses.example: The bond has a maturity of ten years from issue.
senses.exampleCN: 这只债券自发行起十年到期。
senses.why: Finance borrowed the language of ripening: a debt is mature when it has reached the point of payment.
senses.whyCN: 金融借用了「成熟」的说法：债务到了该偿付的时刻，就说它到期。

senses.title: The maturity date
senses.definition: the specific calendar day on which the principal of an instrument must be repaid
senses.definitionCN: 票据本金必须偿还的具体日期
senses.example: Investors marked the maturity date in their calendars.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者把到期日标在日历上。
senses.why: Once a date had to be written down, the abstract state became a fixed appointment.
senses.whyCN: 一旦必须写下一个日期，抽象状态就变成了固定的约定。

senses.title: Yield to maturity
senses.definition: the total return an investor receives if a bond is held until it matures
senses.definitionCN: 债券持有至到期时投资者获得的总回报率
senses.example: The bond's yield to maturity was higher than its coupon rate.
senses.exampleCN: 这只债券的到期收益率高于票面利率。
senses.why: The measure exists because the value of a bond depends on everything received up to and including the final day.
senses.whyCN: 这一指标之所以存在，是因为债券价值取决于到期日及之前收到的全部现金流。

senses.title: Expiry of a contract or policy
senses.definition: the end of the term for which an insurance policy or agreement runs
senses.definitionCN: 保险单或协议的有效期限结束
senses.example: The policy reached maturity and paid out a lump sum.
senses.exampleCN: 这份保单到期并支付了一笔一次性款项。
senses.why: Contracts also have a ripening point, after which the obligations are settled or renewed.
senses.whyCN: 合同同样有一个「熟透」的时点，此后义务结清或续约。

senses.title: Cellular and tissue maturation
senses.definition: the process by which unspecialised cells acquire their adult structure and function
senses.definitionCN: 未特化细胞获得成年结构与功能的过程
senses.example: The culture took three weeks to reach full maturity.
senses.exampleCN: 这组培养物用了三周才完全成熟。
senses.why: In cell biology maturity means differentiation is complete, so the word shifts from the whole body to a single lineage.
senses.whyCN: 在细胞生物学中，成熟意味着分化完成，这个词于是从整个身体转到单一细胞谱系。

senses.title: Soil and ecological maturity
senses.definition: the developed state of a soil profile or an ecosystem that has reached a stable community
senses.definitionCN: 土壤剖面发育完善，或生态系统达到稳定群落的状态
senses.example: The forest had reached maturity after a century without disturbance.
senses.exampleCN: 这片森林在百年无干扰之后达到成熟。
senses.why: Ecology applies the same arc from young to developed, treating a climax community as the mature end point.
senses.whyCN: 生态学套用同样的由幼到熟的弧线，把顶极群落视为成熟的终点。

intro.en: The word comes from Latin maturus, ripe or timely, and its noun maturitas. The Latin origin is clear; the exact date of the English noun's first use is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语中表示「成熟的、适时的」形容词及其名词形式。拉丁来源清楚，英语名词的确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: Maturus described fruit that had ripened and, by extension, anything that had come at the right time.
items.cn: 这个词先形容果实已经成熟，引申指任何「来得正是时候」的事物。

items.en: The same old root is thought to lie behind matutinus, of the morning, so ripeness and early hour share an idea of the right moment.
items.cn: 一般认为同一个古老词根也藏在表示「早晨的」形容词背后，因此「成熟」与「清晨」共享「恰当时刻」这一观念。

items.en: The abstract noun named the state of being ripe or timely, which English took over almost unchanged.
items.cn: 这个抽象名词指成熟或适时的状态，英语几乎原样借入。

items.en: English used the word first for physical ripeness and later for the due date of a debt.
items.cn: 英语先用它指生理成熟，后来才用于债务的到期。

items.en: As bills and bonds became standard instruments, maturity moved from the ripening of fruit to the day a payment falls due.
items.cn: 当票据与债券成为标准工具，「成熟」便从果实成熟转到付款到期的日子。

items.en: The financial use is dated to the modern banking era, but the precise first attestation of the noun is uncertain.
items.cn: 金融用法可系于现代银行时代，但该名词的确切首见时间不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the stem or the finance compounds; the second group names related states of completion.
note.cn: 第一组共享词干或金融搭配；第二组是表示「完成」的相关状态。

entries.definition: The adjective and verb meaning fully developed or to become so.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「成熟的」或「使成熟」的形容词与动词。

entries.definition: The process of becoming mature, especially in biology.
entries.definitionCN: 变为成熟的过程，尤用于生物学。

entries.definition: The state of not yet being mature.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未成熟的状态。

entries.definition: The day on which a financial instrument falls due.
entries.definitionCN: 金融工具到期的那一天。

entries.definition: The return earned by holding a bond to its due date.
entries.definitionCN: 持有债券至到期所获得的回报率。

entries.definition: The state of fruit being ready to eat or harvest.
entries.definitionCN: 果实可以食用或采收的状态。

entries.definition: The stage of being a fully grown person.
entries.definitionCN: 成为完全成年人的阶段。

entries.definition: The completion of growth or formation.
entries.definitionCN: 生长或形成的完成。

entries.definition: The date by which a payment or obligation must be met.
entries.definitionCN: 付款或义务必须履行的日期。

entries.definition: The end of the period for which something is valid.
entries.definitionCN: 某物有效的期限结束。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the arc from fruit to character to finance; abstract ones treat maturity as a threshold rather than a feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着从果实到性格再到金融的弧线展开；抽象联想把成熟看作阈值而非感受。

normal.en: Maturity begins as a fruit word: colour, sugar, texture, ready to pick.
normal.cn: 成熟最初是果实词：颜色、糖度、质地，到了可采摘的程度。

normal.en: The same word then describes a person who can wait and weigh consequences.
normal.cn: 同一个词随后形容能等待、能权衡后果的人。

normal.en: In finance the fruit becomes a bond, and ripe means payable.
normal.cn: 在金融里，果实变成债券，「熟」就是「该付了」。

normal.en: A maturity date is the day the ripening is written into a calendar.
normal.cn: 到期日就是把「成熟」写进日历的那一天。

normal.en: Cells and soils mature too, because every system has a developed end state.
normal.cn: 细胞与土壤也会成熟，因为每个系统都有发育完成的状态。

abstract.en: Maturity is not an age, it is the point where something stops needing to be finished.
abstract.cn: 成熟不是年龄，而是某物不再需要被完成的那一刻。

abstract.en: Every field keeps the same fruit metaphor: unripe, ripening, due.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都保留同一个果实隐喻：未熟、将熟、到期。

abstract.en: A threshold can be crossed quietly, which is why maturity is often noticed only afterwards.
abstract.cn: 阈值可以悄无声息地被跨过，所以成熟往往事后才被察觉。

examples.en: The grapes reach maturity in late September.
examples.cn: 葡萄在九月下旬成熟。

examples.en: The bond has a maturity of five years.
examples.cn: 这只债券期限五年。

examples.en: Emotional maturity matters more than age in this role.
examples.cn: 在这个岗位上，情感成熟比年龄更重要。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「马球里提」——果子熟了才敢办「马球赛」，晚了就到期了：成熟、到期

root: 来自拉丁语 maturus「成熟的、适时的」及其名词 maturitas，经法语进入英语。一般认为表示「早晨的」拉丁形容词也出自同一古老词根，因此「成熟」与「恰当时刻」共享一个观念。金融「到期」义属现代银行时代的引申，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses grow from one image of ripening: the body, the character, the crop, the debt, the date, the return, the contract, the cell and the soil.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都从一个「成熟」意象长出来：身体、性格、作物、债务、日期、回报、合同、细胞与土壤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sugar meter, a rising curve, a crate waiting at the end of the row.
core.cn: 核心意象：糖度计、上升的曲线、地头等着的果筐。

branches.en: THE RIPENING CORE: body and crop both arrive at the point of being fully formed.
branches.cn: 成熟内核：身体与作物都到达完全成形的时点。

branches.en: THE CHARACTER: the same threshold applied to judgement and patience.
branches.cn: 性格层面：同一阈值被用到判断力与耐心上。

branches.en: THE FINANCIAL ARC: due, the date of due, and the return earned by waiting for it.
branches.cn: 金融弧线：到期、到期日，以及等到期所获的回报。

branches.en: THE OTHER COMPLETIONS: a contract's term ends, a cell's differentiation finishes.
branches.cn: 其他完成形态：合同期限结束，细胞分化完成。

branches.en: THE ECOLOGICAL END: a soil profile or a community reaches its developed state.
branches.cn: 生态终点：土壤剖面或群落达到发育完成的状态。

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective plus an abstract noun ending, with English relatives built by negation and by prefixes of time.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁形容词加抽象名词词尾，英语亲属词由否定与时间前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the adjective of ripeness, its abstract noun and the verb of ripening; English adds the ending -ity and the negative and anticipatory prefixes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示成熟的形容词、抽象名词与使成熟的动词；英语加上表示性质的词尾，以及否定与提前的前缀。

items.example: It described fruit at the right moment and then any timely thing.
items.exampleCN: 它先形容恰当时刻的果实，后指任何适时之物。

items.example: The abstract noun passed into English almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 这个抽象名词几乎原样进入英语。

items.example: The verb supplies the English process noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了英语的过程名词与动词。

items.example: It turns the adjective into the name of a state.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成状态名称。

items.example: The shorter form drops the abstract ending.
items.exampleCN: 较短的形容词形式去掉了抽象词尾。

items.example: The ending marks an ongoing process rather than a state.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记进行中的过程而非状态。

items.example: It forms the adjective and noun for what has not ripened.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「尚未成熟」的形容词与名词。

items.example: It marks a birth or event that comes before the due time.
items.exampleCN: 它标记早于应有时刻的出生或事件。

definition_zh: 仁慈；善行；善举；（对人的）恩惠
definition_en: the quality of being kind and generous, or a kind and generous act
core_image: 寒冬里张开的一只递出热汤的手
scene: 灾民排队领粥，施粥棚冒着白汽。 Her quiet beneficence fed the whole village through the famine.
sceneCN: 这里 beneficence 是「善行、恩惠」（第 2 个义项：具体的善举）；句意是她默默的善举让全村人熬过了饥荒。

derivatives.zh: 同根形容词，义为「仁慈的；行善的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「仁慈地」
同根近义词，义为「仁爱；善心」

senses.title: The quality of doing good
senses.definition: the inner quality of wishing and doing good to others
senses.definitionCN: 乐于待人、行善的内在品质
senses.example: The committee honoured a lifetime of beneficence.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会表彰了其一生的仁慈善行。
senses.why: Bene means well and facere means to do, so the quality is well-doing.
senses.whyCN: bene 意为「好」，facere 意为「做」，合起来即「行善」的品质。

senses.title: A kind and generous act
senses.definition: a concrete act of kindness or generosity, often with money or aid
senses.definitionCN: 具体的善行义举，常见于出资施助
senses.example: Her quiet beneficence fed the whole village through the famine.
senses.exampleCN: 她默默的善举让全村人熬过了饥荒。
senses.why: The doing of good hardens into the deed itself.
senses.whyCN: 「行善」的品质凝结为一件件善事本身。

senses.title: The ethical duty to help others
senses.definition: in ethics, the obligation to act for the benefit of others
senses.definitionCN: 伦理学中「应当助人」的原则，如医学伦理的行善原则
senses.example: Medical ethics lists beneficence among its core principles.
senses.exampleCN: 医学伦理把行善原则列为核心原则之一。
senses.why: The moral sense of well-doing becomes a named duty.
senses.whyCN: 「行善」的道德感被确立为一条命名了的义务。

intro.en: Beneficence is Latin bene, well, plus facere, to do, plus the noun suffix -ence.
intro.cn: beneficence 由拉丁语 bene「好」加 facere「做」再加名词后缀 -ence 构成。

items.en: the root dhe- meant to set, to do.
items.cn: 词根 dhe- 意为「放置、做」（重构形式）。

items.en: beneficentia meant well-doing, kindness.
items.cn: 拉丁语 beneficentia 意为「行善、仁慈」。

items.en: beneficence passed through French into learned use.
items.cn: 该词经古法语进入学术用法。

items.en: English borrowed beneficence in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语借入 beneficence。

items.en: it now also names a formal principle in moral philosophy.
items.cn: 如今还作为道德哲学中行善原则的正式名称。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bene- or fic- roots; the near-meaning group gathers kindness words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bene- 或 fic- 词根；近义组汇集仁慈类词。

entries.definition: the doing of evil or harm
entries.definitionCN: 作恶——前缀相反的对照词

entries.definition: a good or helpful result
entries.definitionCN: 益处——同含 bene- 与 fic- 词根

entries.definition: kind goodwill toward others

entries.definition: giving help to the poor

entries.definition: readiness to give freely
entries.definitionCN: 慷慨；侧重大方给予

normalIntro.en: Beneficence is bene plus facere plus -ence: well-doing.
normalIntro.cn: beneficence 是 bene 加 facere 加 -ence：行善之质。

normal.en: The adjective is beneficent.
normal.cn: 形容词是 beneficent。

normal.en: Maleficence is its dark opposite.
normal.cn: maleficence 是它的反面，作恶。

normal.en: Doctors know the principle of beneficence.
normal.cn: 医生熟知行善原则。

normal.en: Benevolence is a close cousin.
normal.cn: benevolence 是近亲词。

normal.en: Do not confuse with benefit, the result.
normal.cn: 不要与表结果的 benefit 混淆。

abstract.en: See steam rising from a soup ladle in winter.
abstract.cn: 看寒冬里汤勺升起的白汽。

abstract.en: Feel a warm coat laid on cold shoulders.
abstract.cn: 感受披上寒肩的暖衣。

abstract.en: Picture an open hand with no string attached.
abstract.cn: 想象一只不附带条件的手。

examples.en: Her quiet beneficence fed the whole village through the famine.
examples.cn: 她默默的善举让全村人熬过了饥荒。

examples.en: The committee honoured a lifetime of beneficence.
examples.cn: 委员会表彰了其一生的仁慈善行。

examples.en: Medical ethics lists beneficence among its core principles.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「杯你的身斯」——一杯热汤递到你身前，这样的人斯文又仁慈。

sensesIntro.en: One noun moves from a kind heart to kind deeds and then to a named moral duty.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个名词，从仁慈之心，落到善行义举，再立为一条道德义务。

core.cn: 核心意象：寒冬里递出热汤的手。

branches.en: a lifetime of beneficence
branches.cn: 一生的仁慈

branches.en: an act of beneficence
branches.cn: 一项善举

branches.en: royal beneficence
branches.cn: 君王的恩典

branches.en: the principle of beneficence
branches.cn: 行善原则

branches.en: out of pure beneficence
branches.cn: 出于纯粹的仁慈

intro.en: Beneficence fixes the doing root fac- inside a noun of quality.
intro.cn: beneficence 把「做」词根 fac- 固定进品质名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pair bene and facere heads this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bene 与 facere 的组合统领这个词族。

items.meaning: kind generosity or a kind act

derivatives.zh: 同根形容词，义为「仁慈的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「仁慈地」

definition_zh: 荣誉；嘉奖；赞扬
definition_en: an award, honour, or strong praise given to someone
core_image: 金杯举过头顶：掌声落在受奖者肩头
scene: 颁奖台上灯光亮起，全场起立，她的名字被念出三次。 The young director received the highest accolade of the festival.
sceneCN: 这里 accolade 是「荣誉、嘉奖」（第 1 个义项：公开授予的奖励或赞誉）；句意为这位年轻导演获得电影节最高荣誉。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加过去分词后缀构成的罕见形容词，义为「受到嘉奖的」
由本词加复数后缀构成，新闻语体常用，义为「接连的荣誉」

senses.title: An award or public praise
senses.definition: an honour, prize, or enthusiastic public approval given for achievement
senses.definitionCN: 因成就而获得的荣誉、奖励或热烈的公开赞许
senses.example: The novel earned accolades from every reviewer.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说赢得了所有评论者的赞誉。
senses.why: The old ceremony of touching the shoulder became the image of any formal act of honour.
senses.whyCN: 古人触肩授爵的仪式，成为一切正式授荣行为的意象来源。

senses.title: The knighting ceremony
senses.definition: in history, the ceremonial embrace or shoulder touch used when making a knight
senses.definitionCN: 历史上册封骑士时拥抱或触肩的仪式
senses.example: The king performed the accolade with a light tap of the sword.
senses.exampleCN: 国王以剑轻触肩膀行册封礼。
senses.why: This is the original sense: the physical gesture on the neck or shoulders that marked a new knight.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义：在颈肩上做出标志新骑士的实体动作。

intro.en: Accolade comes through French from Latin accolade, 'an embrace around the neck', from ad- 'to' and collum 'neck'.
intro.cn: accolade 经法语来自拉丁语 accolade（环颈拥抱），由 ad-（向）与 collum（颈）构成。

items.en: collum meant neck, as in collar.
items.cn: collum 意为颈，如 collar（衣领）。

items.en: accolade meant an embrace about the neck.
items.cn: 拉丁语 accolade 意为环颈拥抱。

items.en: The word named the embrace in the knighting rite.
items.cn: 法语 accolade 指册封骑士礼中的拥抱。

items.en: English borrowed it first for the ceremony itself.
items.cn: 英语借入时首先指册封仪式。

items.en: The sense widened to any honour or loud praise.
items.cn: 词义扩大为任何荣誉或盛赞。

note.en: The first group gathers the neck-root family; the second gathers words for honours.
note.cn: 第一组收「颈」词根词族；第二组收表示荣誉的词。

entries.definition: A band for the neck, from the same Latin stem.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指衣领、项圈。

entries.definition: A neckline of a dress, from the French use of the neck word.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指女装的露颈领口。

entries.definition: An official paper; only spelling-similar, different root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指证书；仅拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Great respect or an award for merit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「荣誉；敬意」。

entries.definition: A prize given for achievement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「奖项」。

entries.definition: An act or statement honouring someone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「颂词；致敬」。

entries.definition: Honours won, pictured as a wreath.
entries.definitionCN: 文学化名词，义为「桂冠；荣誉」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the neck root and the knighting scene; the abstract hooks picture the stage and the applause.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「颈」词根与册封场景；抽象记忆点想象颁奖台与掌声。

normal.en: The root collum means neck: the old accolade embraced the neck.
normal.cn: 词根 collum 意为颈：古老的册封礼拥抱颈部。

normal.en: Compare collar, the band that sits on the neck.
normal.cn: 类比 collar，戴在颈上的衣领。

normal.en: The double c plus single l spelling is worth noting.
normal.cn: 注意双 c 加单 l 的拼写。

normal.en: It is usually plural in news style: accolades.
normal.cn: 新闻语体中常用复数 accolades。

normal.en: The highest accolade means the top honour.
normal.cn: the highest accolade 意为最高荣誉。

abstract.en: Picture a sword touching each shoulder of a kneeling man.
abstract.cn: 想象剑轻触跪者双肩。

abstract.en: Picture a golden cup raised into flashing lights.
abstract.cn: 想象金杯在闪光灯中高举。

abstract.en: Picture an audience rising as one name is read aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被念出时全场起立。

examples.en: The film swept the festival, collecting accolade after accolade.
examples.cn: 这部影片横扫电影节，斩获一项项荣誉。

examples.en: Critics gave the album their warmest accolade of the year.
examples.cn: 评论家把年度最热烈的赞誉给了这张专辑。

examples.en: In medieval courts the accolade was a ritual touch of the sword.
examples.cn: 在中世纪宫廷，册封礼是用剑轻触的仪式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克乐得」——拿奖乐得不行，就是荣誉降临。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ collum（颈）→ accolade（环颈拥抱）→ 古法语册封礼拥抱 → 英语 accolade（册封礼；引申为荣誉嘉奖）

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the medieval neck-embrace ritual to any public honour or praise.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从中世纪的环颈拥抱仪式，扩展到任何公开荣誉或赞誉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands or steel laid on the shoulders to honour
core.cn: 核心意象：以手或剑按在肩颈处以示授荣

branches.en: The original ritual on the neck of a new knight.
branches.cn: 原本施加于新骑士颈肩的仪式。

branches.en: Awards and applause standing in for that touch.
branches.cn: 奖杯与掌声替代了那一下触碰。

branches.en: Both are formal acts that mark someone chosen.
branches.cn: 两者都是标记「被选中者」的正式行为。

branches.en: Critics and festivals hand out modern accolades.
branches.cn: 评论界与电影节颁发现代的荣誉。

branches.en: History keeps the literal sense in armour scenes.
branches.cn: 历史语境保留其字面义于盔甲场景。

intro.en: The word joins the toward-prefix with the neck stem and a noun ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由「向」前缀、「颈」词干与名词结尾组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin collum and accolade are the direct ancestors, so the Latin entries record the noun and the stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 collum 与 accolade 是直接祖先，拉丁条目记录名词与词干。

definition_zh: 可达性；无障碍性；易接近；易理解性；可获得性；负担性
definition_en: the quality of being easy to reach, enter, use, understand or obtain
core_image: 公交站旁新铺的缓坡，轮椅顺着坡推到站台，盲道从路口一直接到车门
scene: 公交站旁新铺了一道缓坡，轮椅能直接推到站台，盲道也从路口接到车门。 The city rebuilt the stop to improve accessibility for wheelchair users.
sceneCN: 这里指为行动不便者消除障碍（第 2 个义项：无障碍性）；句意为该市重建车站以改善轮椅使用者的通行条件。图中可辨识物件：缓坡、站台、盲道、轮椅。

pos.zh: 名词：可达性；无障碍性；易接近；易理解性（不可数）

collocations.zh: 轮椅使用者的无障碍通行
医疗服务的可负担与可及

derivatives.zh: 同一词根的名词与动词，义为「进入；访问；使用权」
由该词根加表示「可……的」形容词词尾构成，义为「可到达的；可理解的」
由该形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「可接近地；易懂地」
由否定前缀加该形容词构成，义为「难以到达的；难以理解的」
由该否定形容词加名词词尾构成，义为「不可达；难以接近」

senses.title: Ease of reaching a place
senses.definition: the quality of a place being easy to reach by road, rail or on foot
senses.definitionCN: 某地可经道路、铁路或步行轻松到达的程度
senses.example: The survey measured accessibility by travel time from the city centre.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查以从市中心出发的通行时间来衡量可达性。
senses.why: The noun turns the act of approaching into a measurable property of a place.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词把「走近」这一动作变成地点身上可测量的属性。

senses.title: Barrier-free access for disabled people
senses.titleCN: 为残障人士消除通行障碍
senses.definition: the design of buildings, transport and services so that disabled people can use them
senses.definitionCN: 把建筑、交通与服务设计得让残障人士也能使用
senses.example: Ramps and lifts improved accessibility across the station.
senses.exampleCN: 缓坡与电梯改善了整座车站的无障碍通行。
senses.why: A place can be physically close and still closed in practice, so the word acquired a design sense.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方可能近在眼前却实际进不去，于是这个词长出了设计义。

senses.title: Digital accessibility
senses.definition: the quality of a website or application being usable with screen readers and other aids
senses.definitionCN: 网站或应用可被读屏软件等辅助工具使用的程度
senses.example: The new portal was audited for accessibility before launch.
senses.exampleCN: 新门户上线前接受了无障碍审查。
senses.why: Digital products repeat the physical problem: information exists but cannot be reached by every user.
senses.whyCN: 数字产品重复了物理世界的问题：信息存在，却不是每个用户都够得着。

senses.title: Ease of understanding
senses.definition: the quality of language or a document being easy to read and follow
senses.definitionCN: 语言或文件易读易懂的程度
senses.example: Plain wording raised the accessibility of the guide for general readers.
senses.exampleCN: 通俗的措辞提高了这份指南对普通读者的易读性。
senses.why: Understanding is another form of reaching, so the same noun covers plain language.
senses.whyCN: 理解是另一种「够得着」，因此同一个名词也管通俗表达。

senses.title: Openness of data and records
senses.titleCN: 数据与记录的开放可获取
senses.definition: the degree to which data or archives are available to researchers and the public
senses.definitionCN: 数据或档案向研究者与公众开放的程度
senses.example: Funders now require accessibility of raw data after publication.
senses.exampleCN: 资助方现在要求论文发表后原始数据可获取。
senses.why: Open science extended the word from buildings to information held in systems.
senses.whyCN: 开放科学把这个词从建筑扩展到系统中保存的信息。

senses.title: Affordability of a service
senses.definition: the degree to which a service is within people's financial reach
senses.definitionCN: 某项服务在人们经济能力范围之内的程度
senses.example: The report links accessibility of care to household income.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把医疗服务的可及性与家庭收入联系起来。
senses.why: If a service cannot be paid for, it cannot be reached, so cost enters the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 如果一项服务付不起，也就是够不着，于是费用进入词义。

senses.title: A legal right of access
senses.definition: the legal entitlement to enter, use or obtain something
senses.definitionCN: 进入、使用或获取某物的法定权利
senses.example: The ruling confirmed accessibility to public records as a statutory right.
senses.exampleCN: 这项裁决确认查阅公共记录是法定权利。
senses.why: Law converts practical reach into an enforceable claim on another party.
senses.whyCN: 法律把实际可达性转成一项可对他人主张的权利。

senses.title: Ease of retrieval in psychology
senses.definition: the readiness with which a memory or concept comes to mind
senses.definitionCN: 记忆或概念在脑中被提取出来的容易程度
senses.example: Repeated exposure increases the accessibility of the concept.
senses.exampleCN: 反复接触会提高该概念在头脑中的可提取性。
senses.why: Cognitive science borrowed the word for how quickly the mind reaches stored information.
senses.whyCN: 认知科学借这个词说明头脑多快能取到储存的信息。

senses.title: Approachability of a person
senses.definition: the quality of a person being easy to talk to or approach
senses.definitionCN: 某人容易交谈、容易接近的程度
senses.example: Her accessibility to junior staff changed the tone of the office.
senses.exampleCN: 她对年轻员工的平易近人改变了办公室的气氛。
senses.why: A person, like a building, can be open or closed to approach.
senses.whyCN: 人像建筑一样，可以对人敞开，也可以拒人于外。

intro.en: Accessibility builds on access, from Latin accessus, a coming near, from accedere, to go to, built from ad-, to, and cedere, to go. The endings -ible and -ity are Latin as well. English formed the noun in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词建在表示「进入」的词根之上。该词来自拉丁语 accessus「走近」，源头是动词 accedere「走向」，由表示「向」的前缀与表示「行走」的词根构成。两个词尾也出自拉丁语。英语在十九世纪构成这个名词。

items.en: The verb meant to go or yield, and it also stands behind proceed, precede and concede.
items.cn: 这个动词意为行走、让出，也是「行进、先于、让步」几个词的源头。

items.en: The compound meant to go towards or approach, adding a prefix of direction.
items.cn: 这个复合动词意为走向、接近，加了表示方向的前缀。

items.en: The noun named an approach or an entrance, and it passed into English as access.
items.cn: 这个名词指接近或入口，进入英语后成为表示「进入」的名词。

items.en: The Latin suffix means that can be done, so accessible means that can be reached.
items.cn: 这个拉丁词尾意为「可以被……的」，因此那个形容词意为可被接近的。

items.en: The Latin suffix turns an adjective into the name of its quality.
items.cn: 这个拉丁词尾把形容词变成表示其性质的名称。

items.en: English formed the noun in the nineteenth century, first for approachability and later for design and data; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪构成这个名词，先指可接近性，后扩展到设计与数据；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the root or the suffix; the second group names neighbouring qualities.
note.cn: 第一组共享词根或词尾；第二组是相邻的性质。

entries.definition: The noun or verb for entering or obtaining.
entries.definitionCN: 指进入或获取的名词或动词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning reachable, usable or easy to understand.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为可到达、可使用或易懂的。

entries.definition: In a reachable or easy manner.
entries.definitionCN: 指以可接近或易懂的方式。

entries.definition: The act of coming into possession or office.
entries.definitionCN: 指就任、取得的行为。

entries.definition: An extra item attached to something larger.
entries.definitionCN: 指附属于较大物件的配件。

entries.definition: The state of being obtainable, with less emphasis on physical reach.
entries.definitionCN: 指可获得的状态，较少强调物理可达。

entries.definition: A technical term for the possibility of being reached.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被到达的技术术语。

entries.definition: How easily a tool or product can be used.
entries.definitionCN: 指工具或产品多容易使用。

entries.definition: The quality of being open to all, especially for information.
entries.definitionCN: 指对所有人开放的性质，多用于信息。

entries.definition: The quality of being within a person's financial reach.
entries.definitionCN: 指在经济能力范围之内。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the verb of going towards, and the practical tests a place or a page must pass.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「走向」这个动词，串起一个地方或一个页面必须通过的实际检验。

normal.en: The root verb means to go, so access is literally a way of going in.
normal.cn: 词根意为行走，所以「进入」字面上就是进去的一条路。

normal.en: A ramp test asks whether a chair can reach the platform, which is accessibility in its plainest form.
normal.cn: 缓坡的检验就是看轮椅能否到站台，这是最朴素的可达性。

normal.en: A screen-reader test asks the same question about a web page.
normal.cn: 读屏软件的检验对网页提出同样的问题。

normal.en: Plain wording is accessibility for readers, because understanding is a way of arriving.
normal.cn: 通俗措辞是给读者的可达性，因为理解也是一种抵达。

normal.en: Affordability belongs here too: a service out of financial reach is out of reach.
normal.cn: 可负担性也归在这里：付不起的服务就是够不着。

abstract.en: Accessibility is a question asked from the far side: can I get there, or only look at it?
abstract.cn: 可达性是从远处提出的问题：我能过去，还是只能看着？

abstract.en: Every door has two states, open and closed, and the noun measures the distance between them.
abstract.cn: 每扇门都有开与关两种状态，这个名词衡量的是两者之间的距离。

abstract.en: A society's accessibility is the sum of the doors it leaves open by design.
abstract.cn: 一个社会的可达性，就是它有意留开的那一扇扇门之和。

examples.en: Accessibility of the site improved after the new footbridge opened.
examples.cn: 新步行桥开通后，该场地的可达性提高了。

examples.en: The report rates accessibility for blind users on every page.
examples.cn: 报告逐页评估了盲人用户的无障碍程度。

examples.en: Accessibility of the archive depends on how the records are catalogued.
examples.cn: 档案的可获取程度取决于记录如何编目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿克塞斯比勒提」——脚下的路能走到、门能推开，就是「可达性、无障碍」：可达性、无障碍性

root: 这个词根来自拉丁语 accessus「走近」，源头是 accedere「走向」，由表示「向」的前缀与表示「行走」的动词构成；表示「可被……的」的形容词词尾与把形容词变成性质名词的名词词尾共同构成这个名词。英语在十九世纪构成该名词，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses carry one idea, reaching, across places, designs, data, language, money, law, memory and people.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项把同一个「够得着」的意思，铺到地点、设计、数据、语言、金钱、法律、记忆与人身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a new ramp at a bus stop, with a wheelchair rolling up to the platform and a tactile path joining it.
core.cn: 核心意象：公交站旁的新缓坡，轮椅推上站台，盲道一路接到车门。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL REACH: travel time and distance decide whether a place is accessible.
branches.cn: 物理可达：通行时间与距离决定一个地方是否够得着。

branches.en: THE REMOVED BARRIER: ramps, lifts and screen readers open what was closed.
branches.cn: 被移除的障碍：缓坡、电梯与读屏软件把关闭的东西打开。

branches.en: THE REACHED INFORMATION: plain language and open data.
branches.cn: 被够到的信息：通俗语言与开放数据。

branches.en: THE ECONOMIC AND LEGAL REACH: a price that can be met, and a right that can be claimed.
branches.cn: 经济与法律的可及：付得起的价格，以及可主张的权利。

branches.en: THE MENTAL AND SOCIAL REACH: a memory that surfaces easily, a person easy to approach.
branches.cn: 心理与社交的可及：容易浮现的记忆，以及容易接近的人。

intro.en: The word is Latin from end to end: a verb of going, a prefix of direction, and two suffixes of possibility and quality.
intro.cn: 这个词从头到尾都出自拉丁语：表示行走的动词、表示方向的前缀，以及分别表示可能与性质的两个词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the verb of going, the prefix, the noun of approach and the two suffixes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示行走的动词、方向前缀、表示接近的名词与两个词尾。

items.example: It also stands behind proceed and concede.
items.exampleCN: 它也是「行进」与「让步」二词的源头。

items.example: It gives the going a direction.

items.exampleCN: 英语把它借为表示进入的名词。

items.example: It marks the possibility of being reached.
items.exampleCN: 它标记「可被接近」的可能性。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a noun.

items.exampleCN: 这个形容词陈述可能性。

items.example: It forms inaccessible, out of reach.

senses.title: The academic researcher
senses.titleCN: 以经济为研究对象的学者
senses.definition: a researcher who studies how economies work and publishes work on the subject
senses.definitionCN: 研究经济体系如何运行、并就此发表成果的研究者
senses.example: As an economist she studies why young firms fail so often.
senses.exampleCN: 作为经济学家，她研究年轻企业为何如此频繁地倒闭。
senses.why: The person suffix marks someone occupied with the field named by the base, and that base first named household management and later the whole economy.
senses.whyCN: 表示人的后缀标记「从事基础词所指领域的人」，而这个词根先指治家，后指整个经济。

senses.title: The professional forecaster
senses.definition: a person paid to forecast output, inflation or employment for a bank, a government or a firm
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于银行、政府或企业，负责预测产出、通胀或就业的人
senses.example: The bank's economist expects inflation to fall below three percent.
senses.exampleCN: 该银行的经济学家预计通胀将降到百分之三以下。
senses.why: Once the discipline acquired predictive tools, the same label covered the people paid to turn those tools into forecasts.
senses.whyCN: 当这门学科有了预测工具，同一个称呼便也覆盖那些受雇把工具变成预测的人。

senses.title: The specialist in a branch
senses.definition: someone working inside a particular branch such as labour, agriculture or development
senses.definitionCN: 在劳动、农业或发展等某一具体分支内工作的人
senses.example: A labour economist studies how wages respond to migration.
senses.exampleCN: 劳动经济学家研究工资如何随人口迁移而变化。
senses.why: The suffix names an occupant of a field, and a field can be narrowed to one branch without changing the label.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀指某一领域的从业者，而领域可以收窄到某个分支，称呼本身不必改变。

senses.title: The policy adviser
senses.definition: a person who translates economic analysis into advice for ministers, central banks or regulators
senses.definitionCN: 把经济分析转化为给部长、央行或监管机构建议的人
senses.example: The economist advised the ministry to phase in the tax over two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经济学家建议该部在两年内分阶段引入这项税。
senses.why: Advice is the applied edge of the discipline, so the person who supplies it is still called by the discipline's name.
senses.whyCN: 建议是这门学科最靠近应用的一端，提供建议的人便仍以学科之名相称。

senses.title: The public commentator
senses.definition: a writer or broadcaster who explains economic events to a general audience
senses.definitionCN: 向普通读者或听众解释经济事件的写作者或广播者
senses.example: The newspaper's economist explained the rate rise in plain language.
senses.exampleCN: 该报的经济学家用平实的语言解释了这次加息。
senses.why: The label can name anyone who speaks from the discipline in public, not only those who research it.
senses.whyCN: 这个称呼可以指任何在公共场合以这门学科发言的人，而不只限于做研究的人。

senses.title: Historical household manager
senses.definition: in earlier use, a person who managed a household and its property
senses.definitionCN: 较早用法中指管理家宅及其财产的人
senses.example: In seventeenth-century usage an economist was the steward of a great house.
senses.exampleCN: 在十七世纪的用法里，经济学家是一座大宅的管家。
senses.why: The Greek base named household management, so the earliest English users applied the person suffix to the one who ran a household.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根本指治家，因此早期英语使用者把这个表示人的后缀加在主持家宅事务的人身上。

senses.title: Historical thrifty person
senses.titleCN: 旧义：善于理财节俭的人
senses.definition: in earlier use, a person skilled in saving and careful with money
senses.definitionCN: 较早用法中指善于储蓄、用钱谨慎的人
senses.example: Her grandfather was called an economist for wasting nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖父因从不浪费而被称作善于理财的人。
senses.why: Household management included frugality, and the label could describe anyone who practised it in daily life.
senses.whyCN: 治家包含节俭，于是这个称呼也能描述在日常生活中实践节俭的任何人。

senses.title: Member of a school of thought
senses.definition: a thinker identified with a particular tradition such as the classical or Keynesian school
senses.definitionCN: 归属于古典、凯恩斯等某一思想传统的思想者
senses.example: The classical economist argued that prices would adjust on their own.
senses.exampleCN: 这位古典经济学家主张价格会自行调整。
senses.why: A discipline organised into rival traditions lets the person label attach to the followers of each tradition.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科若分成相互竞争的传统，表示人的称呼便能附着于各传统的追随者。

intro.en: Economist joins the economy family with the person suffix -ist. Economy came from Greek oikonomia, itself oikos 'household' plus nemein 'to distribute or manage', and passed through Latin oeconomia into English. The suffix came from Greek -istes through Latin -ista and French -iste. The word is not a Latin root with a suffix glued on: its base is Greek in origin and reached English through Latin transcription, and the person suffix arrived by way of Latin and French. The word is generally thought to have appeared in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示经济的词干加上一个表示人的后缀构成，并不是在拉丁词根上直接加后缀：词干源自希腊 oikonomia（由 oikos「家宅」与 nemein「分配、管理」合成），经拉丁 oeconomia 转写进入英语；表示人的后缀则出自希腊 -istes，经拉丁 -ista 与法语 -iste 传来。一般认为这个词在十七世纪出现。

items.en: Oikos meant a house, a household and the property attached to it, the basic unit of ancient domestic life.
items.cn: oikos 指房屋、家宅及附属于它的财产，是古代家庭生活的基本单位。

items.en: Oikonomia joined oikos with nemein 'to distribute, manage', naming the art of running a household, including its slaves, stores and accounts.
items.cn: oikonomia 把 oikos 与表示「分配、管理」的 nemein 结合，指经营家宅的技艺，包括人丁、仓储与账目。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word as oeconomia and widened it from household management to the management of a state or an estate.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该词作 oeconomia，并把范围从治家扩大到治理国家或庄园。

items.en: French économiste named a writer on economic matters in the seventeenth century, and English took the pattern of the word from French.
items.cn: 十七世纪法语 économiste 指撰写经济事务的作者，英语沿用了这个词的构词方式。

items.en: English economist is generally thought to have arisen in the seventeenth century, when it first meant a household manager or a thrifty person rather than a university researcher.
items.cn: 一般认为英语 economist 在十七世纪出现，最初指治家者或节俭的人，而不是大学研究者。

items.en: After political economy was shortened to economics in the nineteenth century, economist settled into its modern sense of a professional analyst of the economy.
items.cn: 十九世纪政治经济学缩称为经济学之后，economist 固定为对经济作专业分析的人这一现代含义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same economy family whose word class or meaning is often confused with the person noun; the near-meaning group gathers analysts who work with numbers but from different angles.
note.cn: 形近组收的是同一经济词族中词性或含义易与「指人名词」混淆的词；近义组收的是同样与数字打交道的分析者，但角度不同。

entries.definition: The system of production and trade in a country or region; it is the base noun, not the person, and it is not a description of a job.
entries.definitionCN: 指一国或一地区的生产与贸易体系；它是基础名词，不指人，也不描述职业。

entries.definition: The name of the academic subject; it looks like a plural but names one field and never one person.
entries.definitionCN: 学科名称；形式像复数，却指一个领域，绝不指某个人。

entries.definition: An adjective describing the economy, as in economic growth; unlike the person noun it cannot be the subject of a sentence about a job.
entries.definitionCN: 描述经济的形容词，如经济增长；与指人的名词不同，它不能作「从事某职业」的主语。

entries.definition: Means saving money or cheap to run; it is close in shape but has nothing to do with the profession.
entries.definitionCN: 意为省钱、运行成本低；外形相近，却与这门职业无关。

entries.definition: An economist who specialises in statistical methods; the broader label also covers those who never run a regression.
entries.definitionCN: 专精统计方法的经济学家；范围更广的称呼也涵盖从不做回归分析的人。

entries.definition: Someone who values shares, bonds or companies; the work is market-facing rather than a study of the whole economy.
entries.definitionCN: 评估股票、债券或公司价值的人；其工作面向市场，而非研究整个经济。

entries.definition: A person trained in collecting and interpreting data; the economist adds a body of theory about incentives and markets.
entries.definitionCN: 受训于收集与解读数据的人；经济学家则另有关于激励与市场的理论体系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here follow the real Greek household root, the Latin transfer, the person suffix and the fixed phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自这个词真实的希腊家宅词根、拉丁转写、表示人的后缀，以及它实际保留的固定搭配。

normal.en: Oikos 'household' plus nemein 'distribute' gives oikonomia, the art of managing a house and its stores.
normal.cn: oikos「家宅」加 nemein「分配」构成 oikonomia，即管理家宅与仓储的技艺。

normal.en: Latin oeconomia widened the household art into the management of a state or estate.
normal.cn: 拉丁 oeconomia 把治家之术扩大到治理国家或庄园。

normal.en: The person suffix -ist, from Greek -istes, marks someone occupied with a field, as in physicist or biologist.
normal.cn: 表示人的后缀出自希腊 -istes，标记从事某领域的人，如物理学家或生物学家。

normal.en: The subject was long called political economy before it was shortened to economics.
normal.cn: 这门学科长期称作政治经济学，后来才缩称为经济学。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the professional sense: chief economist, labour economist, economists' forecast.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出职业义：首席经济学家、劳动经济学家、经济学家的预测。

abstract.en: Picture a single line on a large graph that stands for the mood of millions of households.
abstract.cn: 想象一张大图上的单独一条线，它代表着千百万家庭的处境。

abstract.en: Picture a committee table where one person is asked to say what all those numbers will do next year.
abstract.cn: 想象一张委员会长桌，其中一人被要求说出这些数字明年会怎样。

abstract.en: Picture a candlelit ledger in an old house, kept by the one person trusted to balance it.
abstract.cn: 想象旧宅里一本烛光下的账簿，由唯一被信任能把它做平的人掌管。

examples.en: The economist's model predicts a slowdown in household spending next year.
examples.cn: 这位经济学家的模型预测明年家庭支出将放缓。

examples.en: Government economists were divided over the size of the stimulus package.
examples.cn: 政府的经济学家对刺激方案的规模意见分歧。

examples.en: In the older sense, an economist was simply someone who kept a household in order.
examples.cn: 在较早的含义里，经济学家不过是把家宅打理得井井有条的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一抠呢米斯特」：一位姓米斯特的先生凡事都要一抠到底，于是被称作经济学家。

root: 希腊 oikos「家宅」+ nemein「分配、管理」→ 希腊 oikonomia「治家之术」→ 拉丁 oeconomia（由家宅扩大到国家）→ 法语 économiste → 英语 economist，再加希腊来源、经拉丁与法语传来的表示人的后缀；一般认为十七世纪出现，最初指治家者或节俭者。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: a household is managed, that art is widened to the state, the manager becomes a researcher, and the researcher splits into forecaster, branch specialist, adviser, commentator, school member and finally the older steward and thrifty figure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线展开：先有家宅的经营，这门技艺再扩大到国家，治家者变为研究者，研究者又分化为预测者、分支专家、顾问、解说者、学派成员，最后回到较早的管家与节俭者形象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person at a desk turning a household ledger into a national account.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人坐在桌前，把一本家宅账簿换成一本国民账户。

branches.en: RESEARCH AND FORECAST: the academic who explains the economy and the professional who is paid to say what comes next.
branches.cn: 研究与预测：解释经济的学者，以及受雇判断下一步走势的职业人士。

branches.en: NARROWING AND APPLYING: work inside one branch, then carry that work into advice for ministers and regulators.
branches.cn: 收窄与应用：先在某一分支内做研究，再把研究带进给部长与监管者的建议。

branches.en: PUBLIC VOICE AND OLD STEWARD: the commentator who speaks to readers, and the earlier steward who ran a great house.
branches.cn: 公共言说与旧日管家：面向读者的解说者，以及更早掌管大宅的管家。

branches.en: FRUGALITY: the older figure who saved carefully, the domestic virtue inside the household art.
branches.cn: 节俭：较早那位精打细算的人，是治家之术里的家庭美德。

intro.en: The word reads in three parts: a Greek household root, a Latin transfer of that root, and a Greek-origin person suffix that reached English through Latin and French.
intro.cn: 这个词可分三段读：希腊的家宅词根、该词根的拉丁转写，以及一个经拉丁与法语进入英语、源自希腊的表示人的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin oeconomia and oeconomus are the forms that carried the household idea into medieval and modern European languages.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 oeconomia 与 oeconomus 是把治家观念带入中世纪及现代欧洲语言的形式。

items.meaning: to distribute, to manage, to allot

items.meaningCN: 治家之术，后指公共管理
items.example: Oikonomia named the art before it named a science.

definition_en: the layer of plants covering the ground, or the share of ground that such plants cover
core_image: 从空中俯看，地面被一块块绿色补丁盖住，裸露的土只在缝隙里露出
scene: 从高空俯看，绿色补丁连成片的地方土不易被冲走，补丁破碎的地方沟壑开始出现；研究者用这种差别判断土地退化的程度。 Satellite images show vegetation cover shrinking along the river.

senses.title: The plant layer over the ground
senses.definition: the layer of plants that lies over the soil surface
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖在土壤表面的植物层
senses.example: Thick vegetation cover kept the slope from sliding.
senses.exampleCN: 厚厚的植被覆盖使山坡没有滑动。
senses.why: The phrase joins a mass noun for plants to a noun for a lid: what plants do to soil is throw a lid over it.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把指植物的集合名词与指盖子的名词连在一起：植物对土壤做的事，就是给它盖上一层。

senses.title: The percentage of ground covered
senses.titleCN: 被植物盖住的地面所占的成数
senses.definition: the proportion of an area covered by plants, usually given as a percentage
senses.definitionCN: 一个区域内被植物覆盖的比例，通常按百分数给出
senses.example: Vegetation cover fell from sixty to thirty percent in ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 十年间植被覆盖度从六成降到三成。
senses.why: Once the layer is measured, the phrase shifts from the lid to a number: how much of the ground wears it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这层被测量，短语就从「盖子」转为「数值」：地面有多大比例盖着它。

senses.title: A mapped layer in remote sensing
senses.titleCN: 遥感图上单独画出的一层
senses.definition: the plant layer as a separate class in a satellite or GIS map
senses.definitionCN: 卫星或地理信息图中单独分出的植物图层
senses.example: The map overlays vegetation cover on the rainfall grid.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅地图把植被覆盖叠在降水网格上。
senses.why: Digital mapping turns the living lid into a coloured layer that can be switched on and off beside other layers.
senses.whyCN: 数字制图把这层活盖子变成可与其他图层一起开关的彩色图层。

senses.title: A shield for topsoil
senses.titleCN: 挡雨挡风、护住表土的那层
senses.definition: the layer understood by what it protects, namely the soil beneath it
senses.definitionCN: 从所保护的表土来理解的那一层植物
senses.example: Vegetation cover keeps the topsoil from washing away.
senses.exampleCN: 植被覆盖使表土不被冲走。
senses.why: In soil science the phrase names a service rather than an object: the roots and litter hold grains in place.
senses.whyCN: 在土壤学里，这个短语命名的是一种功能而非物件：根与落叶层把土粒固定住。

senses.title: A cover type or structure
senses.titleCN: 按形态划分的覆盖类别
senses.definition: a class of cover defined by growth form, such as woody or grass cover
senses.definitionCN: 按生长形态划分的覆盖类别，如木本或草本覆盖
senses.example: Woody vegetation cover reacts differently from grass cover.
senses.exampleCN: 木本植被覆盖与草本覆盖的反应不同。
senses.why: Classifying the lid by its builders lets ecologists compare places that look alike from above but differ in species.
senses.whyCN: 按「建造者」给盖子分类，生态学家就能比较从空中看相似、物种却不同的地方。

senses.title: Cover tracked through time
senses.titleCN: 被连续观测以看变化的那层
senses.definition: the layer followed over years to detect gain or loss
senses.definitionCN: 连年跟踪以判断增加或减少的那层植物
senses.example: Repeat flights track vegetation cover after grazing stops.
senses.exampleCN: 停止放牧后，重复航拍跟踪植被覆盖。
senses.why: Monitoring treats the lid as a signal: if it closes over bare ground, the land is recovering.
senses.whyCN: 监测把这层盖子当作信号：它若在裸地上合拢，说明土地正在恢复。

senses.title: Cover restored by protection
senses.titleCN: 经封育、补植而重新长回的那层
senses.definition: the layer rebuilt by fencing, reseeding or grazing control
senses.definitionCN: 通过围封、补播或控制放牧重新长出的植物层
senses.example: Fencing let vegetation cover return within five years.
senses.exampleCN: 围封之后，植被覆盖在五年内恢复。
senses.why: Restoration speaks of the phrase as a goal, something a manager can bring back rather than merely measure.
senses.whyCN: 恢复语境把它当作目标，是管理者能重新带回来的东西，而不只是测量对象。

senses.title: Cover lost through overuse
senses.titleCN: 因过度放牧或开垦而消失的那层
senses.definition: the layer removed by overgrazing, clearing or drought
senses.definitionCN: 因过度放牧、开垦或干旱而丧失的植物层
senses.example: Overgrazing strips vegetation cover from the upper slope.
senses.exampleCN: 过度放牧剥去了上坡的植被覆盖。
senses.why: Loss reverses the lid image: the ground is uncovered again, and every agent of erosion gets direct access.
senses.whyCN: 丧失把盖子的意象倒过来：地面重新裸露，各种侵蚀力量直接触及它。

intro.en: The phrase is modern, but both parts are old: vegetation from Latin vegetare 'to enliven', cover from Latin cooperire 'to cover completely'.
intro.cn: 这个短语是现代组合，两部分都很古老：vegetation 来自拉丁 vegetare「使有生气」，cover 来自拉丁 cooperire「完全盖住」。

items.en: Vegetatio 'growth, a making lively' supplied vegetation, the plant mass of a place.
items.cn: vegetatio「生长、使有生气」提供了 vegetation，即一地的植物整体。

items.en: Cooperire 'to cover wholly' is co- 'together, completely' plus operire 'to close, cover'.
items.cn: cooperire「完全盖住」由 co-「完全」与 operire「关上、遮住」构成。

items.en: Old French covrir gave English cover in the thirteenth century, first as a verb, later as a noun.
items.cn: 古法语 covrir 在 13 世纪给出英语 cover，先作动词，后作名词。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology and remote sensing joined the two words to name the plant layer over soil and its measured share.
items.cn: 20 世纪的生态学与遥感把这两个词连起来，命名土壤之上的植物层及其测得比例。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and root): the exact first use of the compound is not fixed, and the deeper origin of Latin operire is disputed, so any older root offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与词根）：这个复合形式的确切首用年代没有定论；拉丁 operire 的更深来源有争议，凡为其给出的更古老词根都是重构形式。

note.en: Group one contrasts look-alikes built on cover or on the same Latin stem; group two holds the neighbouring terms of land description.
note.cn: 第一组对比由 cover 或同一拉丁词干构成的外形相近词；第二组是土地描述中的邻近术语。

entries.definition: From cover plus -age: the extent something reaches, as insurance coverage; it measures reach, not plants.
entries.definitionCN: 由 cover 加 -age 构成：指某事物达到的范围，如保险覆盖；它量的是范围，不是植物。

entries.tag: same root plain verb or noun
entries.definition: The simple word for putting something over something else; it says nothing about plants.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物盖在另一物上的简单词，不含植物的意思。

entries.definition: From Latin cooperire too, but it means concealed or a hiding place, not a plant layer.
entries.definitionCN: 同样来自拉丁 cooperire，却指隐蔽的或藏身处，不是植物层。

entries.definition: Old French covrir plus lit 'bed': a bedspread, a lid for a bed rather than for soil.
entries.definitionCN: 古法语 covrir 加 lit「床」：床罩，盖的是床不是土。

entries.definition: The full classification of what lies on the ground, including water, rock and buildings; vegetation cover is one class within it.
entries.definitionCN: 对地表一切覆盖物的完整分类，含水、岩石与建筑；植被覆盖只是其中一类。

entries.definition: The share of ground shaded by tree crowns, measured from above; it ignores low plants.
entries.definitionCN: 树冠遮住地面的比例，从上方测量，不计低矮植物。

entries.definition: Low-growing plants that hide bare soil; it names the plants, while vegetation cover also names the measured share.
entries.definitionCN: 遮住裸土的低矮植物；它指植物本身，植被覆盖还指测得的比例。

entries.definition: The plants of an area as a whole; adding cover turns the mass into a layer with a measurable extent.
entries.definitionCN: 一地植物的整体；加上 cover 后，整体变成有可测范围的一层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations are the real parts of the compound and the real terms of ecology.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用这个复合词的真实构成部分与生态学真实术语。

normal.en: vegetation 'plant mass' + cover 'lid': a lid of plants over soil.
normal.cn: vegetation「植物整体」+ cover「盖子」：盖在土上的一层植物。

normal.en: The family: vegetation, cover, coverage, cover crop.
normal.cn: 同族：vegetation、cover、coverage、cover crop。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: vegetation cover change, vegetation cover loss, vegetation cover map.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：植被覆盖变化、植被覆盖丧失、植被覆盖图。

normal.en: Latin cooperire 'to cover wholly' is co- plus operire, so cover already means a complete lid.
normal.cn: 拉丁 cooperire「完全盖住」是 co- 加 operire，可见 cover 本身就含「完全盖上」。

normal.en: Remote sensing treats it as one switchable layer beside rainfall and slope.
normal.cn: 遥感把它当作降水、坡度旁边一个可开关的图层。

abstract.en: Picture a green patchwork quilt whose holes show bare brown soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一床绿色拼布被，破洞里露出褐色的裸土。

abstract.en: Picture a percentage written on that quilt, saying how much of the bed it covers.
abstract.cn: 想象那床被子上写着一个百分数，说明它盖住了床的多少。

abstract.en: Picture a scab forming over a cut in the land until the surface closes.
abstract.cn: 想象土地的一道伤口上结出痂，直到表面合拢。

examples.en: Grazing pressure reduced vegetation cover across the plateau.
examples.cn: 放牧压力使高原各处的植被覆盖减少。

examples.en: The report maps vegetation cover against soil loss.
examples.cn: 报告把植被覆盖与土壤流失对照制图。

examples.en: Willows raised vegetation cover on the sandbank within three seasons.
examples.cn: 柳树在三个季节内提高了沙洲的植被覆盖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「植被 + 盖子」——给土地盖上一层绿被子，还量出盖了多少 → 植被覆盖

root: vegetation 来自拉丁 vegetatio「生长」，cover 来自拉丁 cooperire「完全盖住」（co- + operire）；operire 更深来源有争议。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the lid itself to the percentage it covers, then to its map, its service, its types, its gain, and finally its loss.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「盖子」本身，转到它覆盖的百分比，再到它的图、它的功能、它的类型、它的增加，最后到它的丧失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a green lid laid over bare ground, seen from above as a patchwork.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层盖在裸地上的绿色盖子，从空中看像拼布。

branches.en: LID AND NUMBER: the same phrase names the layer and then the share of ground it hides.
branches.cn: 盖子与数字：同一短语既指那层，也指它遮住的地面比例。

branches.en: MAP AND TYPE: remote sensing makes it a layer, ecology splits that layer into growth forms.
branches.cn: 图层与类型：遥感把它做成图层，生态学再把图层按生长型拆分。

branches.en: SERVICE: the layer is read by what it protects, the topsoil below.
branches.cn: 功能：这层按它所保护的下方表土来理解。

branches.en: GAIN: repeated flights and fencing both ask whether the lid is closing again.
branches.cn: 增加：重复航拍与围封都在问，这层盖子是否重新合拢。

branches.en: LOSS: removing the lid exposes the ground to wind and water.
branches.cn: 丧失：揭开盖子，地面就直接暴露给风与水。

intro.en: The compound is transparent: a Latin noun for plant growth plus a Latin verb for covering, each still productive in English.
intro.cn: 这个复合词是透明的：一个指植物生长的拉丁名词，加一个指覆盖的拉丁动词，两部分在英语中仍能产。

latinIntro.en: Latin vegetatio gives vegetation; Latin cooperire, through Old French covrir, gives cover and coverage.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vegetatio 给出 vegetation；拉丁 cooperire 经古法语 covrir 给出 cover 与 coverage。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使覆盖成为完全覆盖。

items.example: The Latin verb is the core of cover.
